sentences.zh: 姜應麟，字泰符，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yinglin, style Taifu, was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yinglin, styled Taifu, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 父國華，嘉靖中進士。

translations.literal: His father Guohua was a jinshi in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guohua had passed the metropolitan examination in the Jiajing era.

sentences.zh: 歷陜西參議，有廉名。

translations.literal: He served as Shaanxi assistant commissioner and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to be an assistant commissioner in Shaanxi and was known for his probity.

sentences.zh: 應麟舉萬歷十一年進士，改庶吉士，授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Yinglin passed as jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin became a jinshi in Wanli 11, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 貴妃鄭氏有殊寵，生子常洵，詔進封為皇貴妃。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Zheng enjoyed extraordinary favor; she bore Changxun, and an edict advanced her to Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial consort Lady Zheng held exceptional favor. After she bore Changxun, an edict promoted her to Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 而王恭妃育皇長子已五歲，無所益封。

translations.literal: Yet Consort Wang, who had borne the eldest imperial son, now five years old, received no added ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Consort Wang, who had given birth to the eldest imperial son, now five, received no comparable advancement.

sentences.zh: 中外籍籍，疑帝欲立愛。

translations.literal: Within and without the court there was widespread murmuring, and suspicion that the emperor meant to establish his favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread at court and beyond that the emperor intended to name his favorite as heir.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月，應麟首抗疏言：「禮貴別嫌，事當慎始。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year, Yinglin was first to submit a bold memorial, saying: "Rites value separating what is suspect; affairs should be begun with care."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 14, Yinglin led the remonstrance with a memorial: "Ritual demands that suspicious distinctions be kept clear, and affairs must be set right at the outset."

sentences.zh: 貴妃所生陛下第三子猶亞位中宮，恭妃誕育元嗣翻令居下。

translations.literal: The third son born to the consort still ranks below the empress, while the consort who bore the primary heir is instead placed beneath.
translations.idiomatic: The third son born to the favored consort is still ranked below the empress, yet the consort who bore Your Majesty's eldest son is placed beneath her instead.

sentences.zh: 揆之倫理則不順，質之人心則不安，傳之天下萬世則不正，非所以重儲貳、定眾誌也。

translations.literal: Measured against human relations it is not proper; tested against men's hearts it is not secure; transmitted through all ages under Heaven it is not correct—not the way to honor the heir apparent and settle the people's will.
translations.idiomatic: By moral principle it is wrong; in the hearts of men it breeds unease; handed down through the ages it will be judged unjust. This is no way to honor the heir and settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏請俯察輿情，收還成命。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty to look down and heed public sentiment, and to withdraw the completed order.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed public feeling and withdraw this decree.

sentences.zh: 其或情不容已，請先封恭妃為皇貴妃，而後及於鄭妃，則禮既不違，情亦不廢。

translations.literal: If feeling cannot be set aside, then first ennoble Consort Wang as Imperial Noble Consort and only afterward extend the same to Lady Zheng—then ritual is not violated and affection is not cast away.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cannot set affection aside entirely, ennoble Consort Wang as Imperial Noble Consort first and only then Lady Zheng, so that ritual is preserved without denying your feelings.

sentences.zh: 然臣所議者末，未及其本也。

translations.literal: Yet what your servant discusses is the branch, not yet the root.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I have argued touches only the branch, not the root.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲正名定分，別嫌明微，莫若俯從閣臣之請，冊立元嗣為東宮，以定天下之本，則臣民之望慰，宗社之慶長矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to rectify names and fix ranks, to separate suspicion and clarify what is subtle, nothing is better than to bow to the grand secretaries' request and invest the primary heir as Eastern Palace, thereby fixing the foundation of all under Heaven—then the hopes of officials and people will be eased and the fortune of the altars prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly means to set names and ranks aright and to remove every ground for suspicion, you should accept the grand secretaries' plea and invest the eldest son as heir apparent, fixing the foundation of the realm. Then the hopes of your subjects will be answered and the altars secured for long ages.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝震怒，抵之地，遍召大珰諭曰：「冊封貴妃，初非為東宮起見，科臣奈何訕朕！

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the emperor was shaken with rage, dashed it to the ground, and summoning the chief eunuchs all around instructed them: "Enfeoffing the consort was never undertaken with the Eastern Palace in view—how dare the censorial officials slander Us!"
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor flew into a rage and hurled it to the floor. Summoning the chief eunuchs, he said, "Promoting the consort was never about the Eastern Palace—how dare the censorial officials slander me!"

sentences.zh: 」手擊案者再。

translations.literal: " He struck the desk with his hand twice.
translations.idiomatic: " He struck the desk twice with his hand.

sentences.zh: 諸珰環跪叩首，怒稍解，遂降旨：「貴妃敬奉勤勞，特加殊封。

translations.literal: The eunuchs knelt all around and kowtowed; his anger eased somewhat, and he then issued a decree: "The consort has served with reverence and toil; she is specially granted an extraordinary ennoblement."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs knelt in a circle and kowtowed until his anger subsided somewhat. Then he issued a decree: "The consort has served with reverence and diligence and is granted this extraordinary promotion."

sentences.zh: 立儲自有長幼，姜應麟疑君賣直，可降極邊雜職。

translations.literal: Establishing the heir has its order of senior and junior; Jiang Yinglin suspects his ruler of peddling integrity and may be demoted to a miscellaneous post on the farthest border.
translations.idiomatic: Heirship follows seniority by birth. Jiang Yinglin is judged to have accused his sovereign of courting a reputation for blunt honesty and is demoted to a minor post on the remotest frontier.

sentences.zh: 」於是得大同廣昌典史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he received the post of registrar of Guangchang in Datong.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed registrar of Guangchang in Datong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吏部員外郎沈璟、刑部主事孫如法繼言之，並得罪。

translations.literal: Shen Jing, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Sun Rufa, secretary in the Ministry of Justice, spoke next and likewise were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jing, a vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Sun Rufa, a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, followed with similar memorials and were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 兩京申救者疏數十上，皆不省。

translations.literal: Memorials pleading for mercy from both capitals numbered several tens; none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of memorials from both capitals pleaded for clemency, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 自後言者蜂起，鹹執「立儲自有長幼」之旨，以責信於帝。

translations.literal: Afterward remonstrators swarmed forth; all upheld the principle that "establishing the heir follows seniority by birth," holding the emperor to his word.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators then rose in swarms, all invoking the principle that "heirship follows seniority by birth" to hold the emperor to his own decree.

sentences.zh: 帝雖厭苦之，終不能奪也。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was wearied and vexed by it, in the end he could not prevail against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary of the clamor, yet in the end he could not override them.

sentences.zh: 應麟居廣昌四年，量移余幹知縣。

translations.literal: Yinglin remained at Guangchang four years, then was transferred by quota to be magistrate of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: After four years at Guangchang, he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Yugan.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，至京，會吏部數以推舉建言諸臣得重譴，應麟遂不復補。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he came to the capital; it happened that the Ministry of Personnel repeatedly imposed heavy punishments on officials recommended for having remonstrated, and Yinglin therefore was never reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he came to the capital, but the Ministry of Personnel was repeatedly punishing officials who had been recommended after remonstrating, and Yinglin was never given another post.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年。

translations.literal: He lived at home twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起太仆少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was raised to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong came to the throne, he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 給事中薛鳳翔劾應麟老病失儀，遂引疾去。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Xue Fengxiang impeached Yinglin for age, illness, and breach of decorum; he then pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Xue Fengxiang impeached him for age, illness, and breaches of court decorum, whereupon Yinglin pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年卒，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he died and was posthumously made minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chongzhen 3 and was posthumously made minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 從子思睿，字顓愚。

translations.literal: His nephew Si Rui, style Zhuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Si Rui, styled Zhuanyu,

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: was orphaned young and served his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: was orphaned young and served his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 舉天啟二年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Tianqi 2 and was appointed a courier in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年擢御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 明年春，陳天下五大弊：曰加派病民，曰郵傳過削，曰搜剔愈精，頭緒愈亂，曰懲毖愈甚，頹廢愈多，曰督責愈急，蒙蔽愈深。

translations.literal: The next spring he set forth the five great abuses of the realm: extra levies that afflict the people; postal relay service cut too far; the more exacting the search and extraction, the more tangled the threads; the sterner the punishments, the more widespread the decay; the more urgent the supervision, the deeper the concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he listed five great abuses plaguing the realm: supplemental levies that burden the people; postal relay service cut beyond reason; ever finer extraction that only multiplies confusion; ever harsher punishments that breed ever more neglect; and ever tighter supervision that drives ever deeper concealment.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切責。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial offended the throne and brought a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 其冬遣宦官監視邊務，抗疏切諫。

translations.literal: That winter eunuchs were sent to oversee border affairs; he submitted a bold memorial of earnest remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when eunuchs were dispatched to oversee border affairs, he submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 已，劾首輔周延儒以家人周文郁為副將，弟素儒為錦衣，叔父人瑞為中書，受賕行私，請罷斥。

translations.literal: Later he impeached the chief grand secretary Zhou Yanru for making his household retainer Zhou Wenyu a deputy commander, his younger brother Suru an officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and his uncle Renrui a secretary in the Secretariat, accepting bribes and practicing favoritism, and asked that he be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He later impeached Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru for appointing his household retainer Zhou Wenyu deputy commander, his younger brother Suru to the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and his uncle Renrui to the Secretariat, all while taking bribes and showing private favor, and he asked that Zhou be removed.

sentences.zh: 已，論救給事中魏呈潤、御史李曰輔、王績燦。

translations.literal: Later he argued in defense of the supervising secretary Wei Chengrun and the censors Li Yuefu and Wang Jican.
translations.idiomatic: He also pleaded on behalf of the supervising secretary Wei Chengrun and the censors Li Yuefu and Wang Jican.

sentences.zh: 巡按雲南。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to tour and inspect Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，歷指諸弊政，而言：「舉朝拯焚救溺之精神，專用之摘抉細微，而以察吏詰戎予奪大柄僅付二三閹寺。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he enumerated the abuses of government, saying: "The court's spirit of rescuing from fire and saving from drowning is spent entirely on picking at minutiae, while the great powers of inspecting officials and examining troops are entrusted to only two or three eunuch temples."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he listed the abuses of government and said, "The court's spirit of rescuing the realm from crisis is spent entirely on picking at petty details, while the great powers of inspecting officials and examining troops are left to two or three eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 厝火自安，不知變計，天下安望太平！

translations.literal: Sitting beside the fire yet feeling secure, not knowing to change course—how can the realm hope for peace!"
translations.idiomatic: You sit beside the fire yet feel secure and will not change course—how can the realm hope for peace!"

sentences.zh: 」忤旨，切責。

translations.literal: " He offended the will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: " Again he offended the throne and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 還朝，值帝撤還二部總理諸鎮監視內臣。

translations.literal: Returning to court, it happened that the emperor had recalled the eunuchs supervising the border garrisons under the joint direction of the two ministries.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he found that the emperor had recalled the eunuchs whom the two ministries had placed in charge of supervising the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 思睿請並撤監視京營關、寧者。

translations.literal: Si Rui asked that those supervising the capital camps and Shanhai and Ningyuan be withdrawn as well.
translations.idiomatic: Si Rui asked that the eunuchs supervising the capital garrisons and the Shanhai and Ningyuan defenses be withdrawn as well.

sentences.zh: 因詆向來秉政大臣阿承將順之罪，意指溫體仁也。

translations.literal: He thereby denounced the crime of the ministers in power who had fawned and yielded—meaning Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced past chief ministers for fawning and acquiescence, clearly intending Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 體仁二子儼、伉數請囑提學僉事黎元寬。

translations.literal: Tiren's two sons Yan and Kang repeatedly asked the educational intendant Li Yuankuan to intervene on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren's sons Yan and Kang had repeatedly pressed the educational intendant Li Yuankuan for favors.

sentences.zh: 會元寬以文體險怪論黜，遂發其二子私書。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuankuan failed candidates for essays in a dangerous and eccentric style; he then published the two sons' private letters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuankuan failed candidates for essays in a dangerous and eccentric style, he published the two sons' private letters to him.

sentences.zh: 思睿劾體仁縱子作奸，以元寬揭為據。

translations.literal: Si Rui impeached Tiren for indulging his sons in wrongdoing, taking Yuankuan's exposé as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Si Rui impeached Tiren for indulging his sons' misconduct, citing Yuankuan's published letters as proof.

sentences.zh: 體仁謂揭不出元寬手，思睿等群謀排陷。

translations.literal: Tiren said the exposé did not come from Yuankuan's hand and that Si Rui and others had conspired in a faction to entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren claimed the exposé was not Yuankuan's work and that Si Rui and others had conspired to frame him.

sentences.zh: 元寬上疏證明，思睿再劾體仁以「群謀」二字成陷人之阱，但知有子，不知有君。

translations.literal: Yuankuan submitted a memorial to prove the facts; Si Rui again impeached Tiren, saying that with the two words "faction conspiracy" he had made a trap to ensnare men—knowing only his sons, not knowing his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankuan submitted a memorial to verify the facts. Si Rui impeached Tiren again, arguing that by invoking "faction conspiracy" Tiren had turned a trap on others and cared only for his sons, not for his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪俸五月。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and docked his salary for five months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and docked his salary for five months.

sentences.zh: 出視河東鹽政。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect the salt administration of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to inspect the salt administration of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 安邑有故都御史曹於汴講學書院，思睿為置田構學舍，公余親蒞講授。

translations.literal: In Anyi there was a lecture academy of the former censor-in-chief Cao Yubian; Si Rui endowed land, built schoolrooms, and in his spare time personally came to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Anyi stood a lecture academy founded by the former censor-in-chief Cao Yubian. Si Rui endowed land, built schoolrooms, and in his spare time lectured there himself.

sentences.zh: 代還，乞假歸裏。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he asked leave to go home.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended he asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 陳登雲，字從龍，唐山人。

translations.literal: Chen Dengyun, style Conglong, was a native of Tangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dengyun, styled Conglong, came from Tangshan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 除鄢陵知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yanling.

sentences.zh: 政最，征授御史。

translations.literal: His administration was rated highest and he was summoned and made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his administration was rated highest, he was summoned to the capital and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 出按遼東，疏陳安攘十策，又請速首功之賞。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Liaodong, he memorialized ten policies for pacification and control, and also asked that rewards for first merit be hastened.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect Liaodong, he memorialized ten policies for pacifying the frontier and urged that rewards for the first victories be granted without delay.

sentences.zh: 改巡山西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tour Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to tour Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 還朝，會廷臣方爭建儲。

translations.literal: Returning to court, it happened that the court officials were contending over establishing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the court was embroiled in the struggle over investing the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 登雲謂議不早決，由貴妃家陰沮之。

translations.literal: Dengyun said the debate had not been settled early because the consort's family secretly obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyun argued that the delay came from the consort's clan working behind the scenes to block a decision.

sentences.zh: 十六年六月，遂因災異抗疏，劾妃父鄭承憲，言：「承憲懷禍藏奸，窺覬儲貳。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixteenth year he therefore submitted a bold memorial on account of calamities and anomalies, impeaching the consort's father Zheng Chengxian, saying: "Chengxian harbors disaster and hides treachery, coveting the heir apparent's place."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Wanli 16 he seized on omens and calamities to submit a bold memorial impeaching the consort's father Zheng Chengxian: "Chengxian harbors malice and hides treachery while coveting the heir's position."

sentences.zh: 日與貂珰往來，綢繆杯酌，且廣結山人、術士、緇黃之流。

translations.literal: Daily he goes back and forth with sable-capped eunuchs, intimate in cups and toasts, and widely befriends recluses, diviners, and monks and priests.
translations.idiomatic: He consorts daily with court eunuchs over wine, and cultivates recluses, diviners, monks, and Daoist priests on every side.

sentences.zh: 曩陛下重懲科場冒籍，承憲妻每揚言事由己發，用以恐喝勛貴，簧鼓朝紳。

translations.literal: Formerly when Your Majesty heavily punished false registration in the examinations, Chengxian's wife would each time proclaim that the matter had been exposed through her, using it to intimidate the meritorious nobles and to drum up the court gentry.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty punished examination fraud, Chengxian's wife boasted that each exposure came through her, using that claim to intimidate the nobility and sway court officials.

sentences.zh: 不但惠安遭其虐焰，即中宮與太后家亦謹避其鋒矣。

translations.literal: Not only did Huian suffer her cruel flame—even the empress and the empress dowager's clan carefully avoided her edge.
translations.idiomatic: Not only did Lady Huian suffer under her tyranny; even the empress and the empress dowager's clan were careful to avoid her wrath.

sentences.zh: 陛下享國久長，自由敬德所致，而承憲每對人言，以為不立東宮之效。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's long enjoyment of the realm is naturally due to reverent virtue, yet Chengxian tells people it is the effect of not establishing the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's long reign owes to your own virtue, yet Chengxian tells others it is because the Eastern Palace has not been established.

sentences.zh: 幹撓盛典，蓄隱邪謀，他日何所不至。

translations.literal: He interferes with great rites and harbors hidden evil designs—what may he not reach to in days to come?
translations.idiomatic: He meddles in the great rites of state and nurses hidden designs—what limit will there be to his ambitions?

sentences.zh: 茍不震奮乾剛，斷以大義，雖日避殿撤樂、素服停刑，恐天心未易格，天變未可弭也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not rouse the firmness of Heaven and decide by great principle, though you daily avoid the hall, withdraw music, wear plain dress, and suspend punishments, I fear Heaven's heart will not easily be moved and Heaven's changes will not be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Your Majesty rouses your firm resolve and acts on principle, no amount of avoiding the hall, withdrawing music, wearing plain dress, or suspending punishments will move Heaven's heart or still these omens.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，貴妃、承憲皆怒，同列亦為登雲危，帝竟留中不下。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the consort and Chengxian were both angry; colleagues also feared for Dengyun, yet the emperor kept it in the palace and did not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the consort and Chengxian were furious. Colleagues feared for Dengyun's safety, but the emperor shelved the memorial and never acted on it.

sentences.zh: 久之，疏論吏部尚書陸光祖，又論貶四川提學副使馮時可，論罷應天巡撫李淶、順天巡撫王致祥，又論禮部侍郎韓世能、尚書羅萬化、南京太仆卿徐用檢。

translations.literal: After a long while he memorialized against the Minister of Personnel Lu Guangzu, also argued for demoting the Sichuan educational vice commissioner Feng Shike, argued to dismiss the Yingtian grand coordinator Li Yuan and the Shuntian grand coordinator Wang Zhixiang, and again argued against the vice minister of Rites Han Shineng, the minister Luo Wanhua, and the Nanjing vice minister of the Imperial Stud Xu Yongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In time he memorialized against Minister of Personnel Lu Guangzu, urged the demotion of Sichuan educational vice commissioner Feng Shike, called for the dismissal of the Yingtian grand coordinator Li Yuan and the Shuntian grand coordinator Wang Zhixiang, and attacked Vice Minister of Rites Han Shineng, Minister Luo Wanhua, and Nanjing vice minister of the Imperial Stud Xu Yongjian.

sentences.zh: 朝右皆憚之。

translations.literal: Those in power at court all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful at court all feared him.

sentences.zh: 時方考選科道，登雲因疏言：「近歲言官，壬午以前怵於威，則摧剛為柔；

translations.literal: At the time censorial posts were under examination and selection; Dengyun therefore memorialized, saying: "In recent years among remonstrating officials, before renshen they were cowed by authority and so broke the firm into the soft;"
translations.idiomatic: While censorial posts were under review, Dengyun memorialized: "In recent years, before the renshen year remonstrators were cowed by power and bent their firmness into compliance;"

sentences.zh: 壬午以後昵於情，則化直為佞。

translations.literal: "after renshen they grew intimate with favor and so turned the straight into flattery."
translations.idiomatic: "after renshen they grew intimate with favor and turned honest bluntness into flattery."

sentences.zh: 其間豈無剛直之人，而弗勝齟齬，多不能安其身。

translations.literal: Among them were there not firm and upright men? Yet unable to overcome friction, most could not keep themselves secure.
translations.idiomatic: There were still upright men among them, but unable to endure the friction, most could not keep their posts.

sentences.zh: 二十年來，以剛直擢京卿者，百止一二耳。

translations.literal: In twenty years, of those promoted to capital ministers for firm uprightness, perhaps one or two in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In twenty years scarcely one or two in a hundred promotions to capital minister went to men noted for upright bluntness.

sentences.zh: 背公植黨，逐嗜乞憐，如所謂『七豺』、『八狗』者，言路顧居其半。

translations.literal: Those who betray the public and form factions, who chase appetites and beg for favor—such as the so-called "Seven Jackals" and "Eight Dogs"—the remonstrating path instead holds half of them.
translations.idiomatic: Men who betray the public good, form factions, and fawn for favor—the so-called "Seven Jackals" and "Eight Dogs"—now fill half the remonstrating posts.

sentences.zh: 夫臺諫為天下持是非，而使人賤辱至此，安望其抗顏直繩，為國家鋤大奸、殲巨蠹哉！

translations.literal: The censorate and remonstrance bureaus uphold right and wrong for all under Heaven—yet when men are debased and humiliated to this degree, how can one expect them to hold their countenance and apply the straight cord, rooting out great traitors and destroying huge vermin for the state!
translations.idiomatic: The censorate exists to uphold right and wrong for the realm, yet when remonstrators are debased and humiliated to this point, how can we expect them to speak boldly and purge great traitors and corruption from the state?

sentences.zh: 與其誤用而斥之，不若慎於始進。

translations.literal: Rather than misuse them and then cast them out, better to be careful at the outset of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Better to choose remonstrators carefully at the outset than to appoint the wrong men and cast them out afterward.

sentences.zh: 」因條數事以獻。

translations.literal: " He then set forth several matters and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then listed several recommendations and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 出按河南。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to inspect Henan.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: That year famine was severe and men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Famine that year was so severe that people resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 副使崔應麟見民啖澤中雁矢，囊示登雲，登雲即進之於朝。

translations.literal: The vice commissioner Cui Yinglin saw the people eating wild-goose droppings from the marshes; he bagged some to show Dengyun, and Dengyun at once presented them at court.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Cui Yinglin saw people eating wild-goose droppings gathered from the marshes. He bagged a sample for Dengyun, who immediately sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝立遣寺丞鐘化民賫帑金振之。

translations.literal: The emperor at once sent the temple director Zhong Huamin bearing treasury funds to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately dispatched the temple director Zhong Huamin with treasury funds for relief.

sentences.zh: 登雲巡方者三，風裁峻厲。

translations.literal: Dengyun toured the regions three times; his manner was stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyun toured the provinces three times, and his conduct was stern and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 以久次當擢京卿，累寢不下，遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: By long service he should have been promoted to a capital minister, but the matter was repeatedly shelved; he then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Long service entitled him to promotion to a capital ministry, but the appointment was repeatedly shelved. He pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 羅大纮，字公廓，吉水人。

translations.literal: Luo Dahong, style Gongkuo, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Dahong, styled Gongkuo, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 14.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月，遷禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Wanli 19 he was made supervising secretary in the Rites Bureau.

sentences.zh: 甫拜命，即上《定制書》數千言。

translations.literal: As soon as he received appointment he submitted a "Book on Established Regulations" of several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office he submitted a memorial of several thousand words entitled "On Established Regulations."

sentences.zh: 已，復言視朝宜勤，語皆切直。

translations.literal: Later he again said that attendance at court should be diligent; his words were all earnest and blunt.
translations.idiomatic: He later urged that the emperor attend court more diligently, speaking with blunt earnestness throughout.

sentences.zh: 先有詔以二十年春冊立東宮，至是工部主事張有德以預備儀物請。

translations.literal: An edict had earlier set the spring of the twentieth year for investing the Eastern Palace; at this time Zhang Youde, a secretary in the Ministry of Works, requested preparations for the ritual objects.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had set the spring of Wanli 20 for investing the heir apparent. Now Zhang Youde, a secretary in the Ministry of Works, requested funds to prepare the ritual objects.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命奪俸三月，更緩冊立事。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered his salary docked for three months, further delaying the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered, docked his salary for three months, and further delayed the investiture.

sentences.zh: 尚書曾同亨請如前詔，忤旨，切讓。

translations.literal: The minister Zeng Tongheng asked that the earlier edict be followed; he offended the will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zeng Tongheng asked that the earlier edict be honored. He offended the throne and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 大纮復以為言，詔奪俸如有德。

translations.literal: Dahong spoke again on the matter; an edict docked his salary as with Youde.
translations.idiomatic: Dahong spoke up again, and an edict docked his salary as it had Zhang Youde's.

sentences.zh: 大學士許國、王家屏連署閣臣名，乞收新命，納諸臣請，帝益怒。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries Xu Guo and Wang Jiaping jointly signed the names of the inner cabinet, begging that the new order be withdrawn and the officials' request accepted; the emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Xu Guo and Wang Jiaping jointly signed a memorial asking that the new order be withdrawn and the officials' plea accepted. The emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 首輔申時行方在告，聞帝怒，乃密揭言：「臣雖列名公疏，實不與知。

translations.literal: The chief grand secretary Shen Shixing was then on leave; hearing of the emperor's anger, he submitted a secret memorial saying: "Though your servant's name was listed on the public memorial, in truth I had no part in it."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing was on leave at the time. Hearing of the emperor's anger, he submitted a secret memorial: "Although my name appeared on the joint memorial, I had no knowledge of it."

sentences.zh: 」帝喜，手詔褒答，而揭與詔俱發禮科。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and personally drafted an edict of praise in reply, but the secret memorial and the edict were both sent to the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased and drafted a personal reply of praise, but both the secret memorial and the reply were routed to the Rites Bureau.

sentences.zh: 故事，閣臣密揭無發科者。

translations.literal: By precedent, secret memorials of inner-cabinet ministers were not sent to the censorial bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, grand secretaries' secret memorials were not routed to the censorial bureaus.

sentences.zh: 時行慚懼，亟謀之禮科都給事中胡汝寧，遣使取揭。

translations.literal: Shixing was ashamed and afraid; he urgently consulted Hu Runing, chief supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau, and sent an envoy to retrieve the secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing was ashamed and alarmed. He urgently consulted Hu Runing, chief supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau, and sent an envoy to retrieve the memorial.

sentences.zh: 時獨大纮守科，使者紿取之。

translations.literal: At the time only Dahong was on duty in the bureau; the envoy deceived him and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dahong was on duty at the bureau. The envoy deceived him and took the memorial away.

sentences.zh: 及往索，時行留不發。

translations.literal: When Dahong went to demand it back, Shixing kept it and would not release it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dahong went to demand it back, Shixing kept it and refused to release it.

sentences.zh: 大纮乃抗疏曰：「臣奉職無狀，謹席稿以待。

translations.literal: Dahong then submitted a bold memorial, saying: "Your servant has performed his office without merit and respectfully spreads out his draft to await punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Dahong then submitted a bold memorial: "Your servant has failed in his office and awaits punishment."

sentences.zh: 獨念時行受國厚恩，乃內外二心，藏奸蓄禍，誤國賣友，罪何可勝言。

translations.literal: Yet I reflect that Shixing has received the state's deep grace, yet harbors two hearts within and without, hiding treachery and storing disaster, misleading the state and betraying friends—his crimes are beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shixing has received the state's deepest favor while harboring divided loyalties, concealing treachery, misleading the state, and betraying his colleagues—crimes beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 夫時行身雖在告，凡翰林遷改之奏，皆儼然首列其名，何獨於建儲一事深避如此。

translations.literal: Though Shixing's person was on leave, every memorial for Hanlin transfers still solemnly placed his name first—why alone on establishing the heir does he avoid so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Though Shixing was on leave, every memorial for Hanlin promotions still listed his name first. Why does he avoid the heir question so completely?

sentences.zh: 縱陛下赫然震怒，加國等以不測之威，時行亦當與分過。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty were suddenly enraged and imposed unforeseen severity on Guo and the others, Shixing ought still to share the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty were to punish Xu Guo and the others severely, Shixing ought still to share the blame.

sentences.zh: 況陛下未嘗怒，而乃沮塞睿聰，搖動國本，茍自獻其乞憐之術，而遏主上悔悟之萌，此臣之所大恨也。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty had not yet been angry, yet he blocked your sage understanding, shook the foundation of the state, and basely offered his art of begging favor while checking the sprouting of your sovereign repentance—this is what your servant most hates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty had not even been angry. He blocked your judgment, shook the foundations of the state, and used fawning tactics to choke off your repentance—this is what I most deplore.

sentences.zh: 假令國等得請，將行慶典而恩澤加焉，時行亦辭之乎？

translations.literal: Suppose Guo and the others had their request granted and the celebration were held with favors bestowed—would Shixing decline them as well?
translations.idiomatic: If Xu Guo and the others had succeeded and the celebration proceeded with honors granted, would Shixing have declined his share?

sentences.zh: 蓋其私心妄意陛下有所牽系，故陽附廷臣請立之議，而陰緩其事，以為自交宮掖之謀。

translations.literal: In his private heart he wrongly supposed Your Majesty was constrained, and so outwardly joined the court officials' plea to establish the heir while inwardly delaying the matter—a scheme to curry favor with the inner palace himself.
translations.idiomatic: In private he assumed Your Majesty was constrained. Outwardly he joined the plea to invest the heir; inwardly he delayed it—a scheme to win favor in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 使請之而得，則明居羽翼之功；

translations.literal: If the request succeeded, he would openly claim the merit of aiding wings;
translations.idiomatic: If the plea succeeded, he could claim credit openly;

sentences.zh: 不得，則別為集菀之計。

translations.literal: if it failed, he would make another plan of gathering to the favored grove.
translations.idiomatic: if it failed, he had another plan to gather support elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 其操此術以愚一世久矣，不圖今日乃發露之也。

translations.literal: He has wielded this art to deceive the age for long; who expected it would be exposed today.
translations.idiomatic: He has used this trick to deceive the court for years. Who expected it would be exposed today?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝震怒，命貶邊方雜職。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the emperor was shaken with rage and ordered him demoted to a miscellaneous post on the border.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor was enraged and ordered him demoted to a minor post on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 俄以六科鐘羽正等論救，斥為民，羽正等奪俸。

translations.literal: Soon the six bureaus, Zhong Yuzheng and others, pleaded for mercy; he was dismissed to commoner status and Yuzheng and the others had their salaries docked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhong Yuzheng and others of the six bureaus pleaded for him. Dahong was reduced to commoner status, and they had their salaries docked.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人黃正賓復抗疏力詆時行。

translations.literal: The Secretariat drafter Huang Zhenbin again submitted a bold memorial fiercely denouncing Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Huang Zhenbin submitted another bold memorial fiercely denouncing Shixing.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下獄拷訊，斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, had him imprisoned and interrogated under torture, and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered, had him imprisoned and tortured, and dismissed him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 時行亦不安，無何，竟引去。

translations.literal: Shixing too was ill at ease; before long he finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing too was uneasy and soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 大纮誌行高卓。

translations.literal: Dahong's will and conduct were lofty and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Dahong's character and conduct were exceptionally high-minded.

sentences.zh: 鄉人以配裏先達羅倫、羅洪先，號為「三羅」。

translations.literal: His townspeople paired him with the local forebears Luo Lun and Luo Hongxian, calling them the "Three Luos."
translations.idiomatic: His countrymen ranked him with the local worthies Luo Lun and Luo Hongxian as the "Three Luos."

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 正賓，歙人。

translations.literal: Zhenbin was a native of She.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenbin came from She county.

sentences.zh: 以貲為舍人，直武英殿。

translations.literal: By purchase of office he became a drafter and served in the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as a Secretariat drafter and served in the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 恥由貲入官，思樹奇節，至是遂見推清議。

translations.literal: Ashamed of entering office by purchase, he sought to establish an extraordinary reputation; by this time he was acclaimed by pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of having bought his way into office, he sought to distinguish himself by moral courage and was now acclaimed by the moral critics of the day.

sentences.zh: 後李三才、顧憲成鹹與遊，益有聲士大夫間。

translations.literal: Later Li Sancai and Gu Xiancheng both associated with him, and his reputation among scholar-officials grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Later he associated with Li Sancai and Gu Xiancheng, and his reputation among scholar-officials grew.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，起故官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong came to the throne, he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚寶少卿，引病歸。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Seals and pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Seals, then pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢下汪文言獄，詞連正賓。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian prosecuted the Wang Wenyan case, and the indictment implicated Zhenbin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian prosecuted the Wang Wenyan case, Zhenbin was implicated.

sentences.zh: 坐贓千金，遣戍大同。

translations.literal: Convicted of a thousand in gold in graft, he was sent in exile to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of accepting a thousand taels in bribes, he was exiled to Datong.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chongzhen succeeded, his office was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年六月，魏黨徐大化、楊維垣已罷官，猶潛居輦下，交通奄寺，正賓在都，抗疏發其奸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Chongzhen, the Wei faction members Xu Dahua and Yang Weiyuan had already been dismissed from office yet still lurked below the imperial carriage, communicating with eunuch temples; Zhenbin was in the capital and submitted a bold memorial exposing their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chongzhen 1, Wei faction members Xu Dahua and Yang Weiyuan had been dismissed but still lurked in the capital, dealing with eunuchs. Zhenbin submitted a bold memorial exposing them.

sentences.zh: 勒兩人歸田裏，都人快之。

translations.literal: He compelled the two men to return to their fields; the people of the capital rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were forced to return home, to the delight of the capital.

sentences.zh: 而疏有「潛通宦寺」語，帝令指名。

translations.literal: Yet the memorial contained the phrase "secretly communicating with eunuch temples," and the emperor ordered specific names.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial spoke of "secret dealings with eunuchs," and the emperor ordered him to name them.

sentences.zh: 正賓以趙倫、於化龍對。

translations.literal: Zhenbin named Zhao Lun and Yu Hualong in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenbin named Zhao Lun and Yu Hualong.

sentences.zh: 帝以其妄，斥回籍。

translations.literal: The emperor judged him reckless and sent him back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged his charges reckless and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 李獻可，字堯俞，同安人。

translations.literal: Li Xianke, style Yaoyu, was a native of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianke, styled Yaoyu, came from Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 11.

sentences.zh: 除武昌推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 課最，征授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: His evaluation was highest; he was summoned and made supervising secretary in the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When his evaluation was rated highest, he was summoned and made supervising secretary in the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 屢遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月，偕六科諸臣疏請豫教，言：「元子年十有一矣，豫教之典當及首春舉行。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twentieth year, together with the officials of the six bureaus he memorialized requesting early instruction, saying: "The primary son is already eleven; the rite of early instruction should be held in the first spring."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wanli 20, he joined the six bureaus in memorializing for the heir's early instruction: "The eldest son is already eleven. The rite should be held in the coming spring."

sentences.zh: 倘謂內庭足可誦讀，近侍亦堪輔導，則禁闥幽閑，豈若外朝之清肅；

translations.literal: "If one says the inner court suffices for recitation and reading and close attendants can also tutor, then the secluded inner gates—how can they compare with the clarity and solemnity of the outer court;"
translations.idiomatic: "If the inner court is deemed sufficient for study and close attendants adequate as tutors, how can the seclusion of the inner palace compare with the dignity of the outer court;"

sentences.zh: 內臣忠敬，何如師保之尊嚴。

translations.literal: "how can inner eunuchs' loyalty and reverence compare with the dignity of tutors and guardians."
translations.idiomatic: "and how can the loyalty of eunuchs compare with the authority of proper tutors and guardians?"

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝大怒，摘疏中誤書弘治年號，責以違旨侮君，貶一秩調外，余奪俸半歲。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angry, picked out a mistaken writing of the Hongzhi reign in the memorial, and rebuked him for defying the will and insulting the sovereign; he was demoted one rank and transferred outside, the rest had salaries docked half a year.
translations.idiomatic: " When it arrived, the emperor was furious. Seizing on a mistaken reference to the Hongzhi reign, he accused them of defying his will and insulting the throne. Xianke was demoted one rank and transferred out; the others had their salaries docked for half a year.

sentences.zh: 大學士王家屏封還禦批，帝益不悅。

translations.literal: The grand secretary Wang Jiaping returned the imperial rescript sealed; the emperor was still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping returned the imperial rescript unopened, which displeased the emperor still more.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中鐘羽正言：「獻可之疏，臣實贊成之，請與同謫。

translations.literal: Zhong Yuzheng, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau, said: "Xianke's memorial—your servant in truth approved it; I ask to be banished with him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yuzheng, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau, said, "I approved Xianke's memorial. I ask to be punished with him."

sentences.zh: 」吏科給事中舒弘緒亦言「言官可罪，豫教必不可不行」。

translations.literal: " The supervising secretary Shu Hongxu of the Personnel Bureau also said, "Remonstrating officials may be punished, but early instruction absolutely cannot be omitted."
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising secretary Shu Hongxu added, "Punish the remonstrators if you must, but early instruction cannot be postponed."

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，出弘緒南京，而羽正及獻可並以雜職徙邊方。

translations.literal: The emperor was still angrier, sent Hongxu to Nanjing, and both Yuzheng and Xianke were transferred to the border as miscellaneous officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still. Hongxu was sent to Nanjing; Yuzheng and Xianke were transferred to minor posts on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯論救，被旨譙讓。

translations.literal: The grand secretary Zhao Zhigao pleaded for mercy and received an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao pleaded for them and was rebuked by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 吏科右給事中陳尚象復爭之，坐斥為民。

translations.literal: Chen Shangxiang, right supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau, argued again and was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shangxiang, right supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau, argued again and was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 戶科左給事中孟養浩，御史鄒德泳，戶兵刑工四科都給事中丁懋遜、張棟、吳之佳、楊其休，禮科左給事中葉初春，各上疏救。

translations.literal: Meng Yanghao, left supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau; the censor Zou Deyong; the chief supervising secretaries of the four bureaus Ding Maoxun, Zhang Dong, Wu Zhijia, and Yang Qixiu; and Ye Chuchun, left supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau—each submitted memorials of rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yanghao, Zou Deyong, Ding Maoxun, Zhang Dong, Wu Zhijia, Yang Qixiu, and Ye Chuchun each submitted memorials pleading for clemency.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，廷杖養浩百，除其名。

translations.literal: The emperor was still angrier; Yanghao was beaten a hundred times at court and his name removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger mounted. Yanghao was beaten a hundred strokes at court and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 德泳、懋遜等六人並貶一秩，出之外。

translations.literal: Deyong, Maoxun, and the other six were all demoted one rank and sent outside.
translations.idiomatic: Deyong, Maoxun, and six others were demoted one rank and sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 獻可、羽正、弘緒亦除名。

translations.literal: Xianke, Yuzheng, and Hongxu also had their names removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke, Yuzheng, and Hongxu were also struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝一怒而斥諫官十一人，朝士莫不駭嘆，然諫者卒未已。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor in one burst of anger dismissed eleven remonstrating officials; court gentlemen were all struck with awe, yet remonstrators in the end did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In a single fit of anger the emperor punished eleven remonstrators. The court was appalled, yet the remonstrance did not end.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎董嗣成、御史賈名儒特疏爭之，御史陳禹謨、吏科左給事中李周策亦偕其僚論諫。

translations.literal: Dong Sicheng, vice director in the Ministry of Rites, and the censor Jia Mingru specially memorialized in dispute; the censor Chen Yumo and Li Zhouce, left supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau, also joined their colleagues in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Sicheng and Jia Mingru submitted special memorials of protest. Chen Yumo and Li Zhouce joined their colleagues in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝怒加甚，奪嗣成職，名儒謫邊方，德泳、懋遜等鹹削籍，禹謨等停俸有差。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger increased; Sicheng's office was taken, Mingru banished to the border, Deyong, Maoxun, and the others all struck from the rolls, and Yumo and the others had salaries suspended in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath deepened. Sicheng was dismissed, Mingru exiled, Deyong and Maoxun struck from the rolls, and Yumo and others had their salaries suspended in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李長春等亦疏諫，帝復詰讓。

translations.literal: Li Changchun, minister of Rites, and others also memorialized in remonstrance; the emperor again rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Changchun and others remonstrated as well and were rebuked again.

sentences.zh: 獻可等遂廢於家。

translations.literal: Xianke and the others were then left unused at home.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke and the others were left in retirement.

sentences.zh: 久之，吏部尚書蔡國珍、侍郎楊時喬先後請收敘，鹹報寢。

translations.literal: After a long while, Cai Guozhen, minister of Personnel, and Vice Minister Yang Shiqiao successively asked that they be recalled and reappointed; all were reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Ministers Cai Guozhen and Yang Shiqiao asked that they be recalled, but each request was shelved.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，錄先朝言事諸臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, the former dynasty's remonstrating officials were recorded for honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign, officials who had remonstrated in the previous reign were honored.

sentences.zh: 獻可已前卒，詔贈光祿卿。

translations.literal: Xianke had already died earlier; an edict posthumously made him minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke had already died. An edict posthumously made him minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 弘緒、名儒皆獻可同年進士。

translations.literal: Hongxu and Mingru were both jinshi in the same year as Xianke.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu and Mingru had been jinshi in the same year as Xianke.

sentences.zh: 尚象、懋遜、之佳、初春、其休、嗣成皆萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: Shangxiang, Maoxun, Zhijia, Chuchun, Qixiu, and Sicheng were all jinshi in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxiang, Maoxun, Zhijia, Chuchun, Qixiu, and Sicheng had all been jinshi in Wanli 8.

sentences.zh: 弘緒，通山人。

translations.literal: Hongxu was a native of Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu came from Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士改給事中。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was changed to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from Hanlin bachelor to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 尚象，都勻人。

translations.literal: Shangxiang was a native of Duyun.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxiang came from Duyun.

sentences.zh: 以中書舍人為給事中。

translations.literal: From Secretariat drafter he became supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Secretariat drafter to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾罷尚書沈鯉，為士論所非。

translations.literal: He once impeached and brought down Minister Shen Li, which scholar opinion condemned.
translations.idiomatic: He had once impeached Minister Shen Li out of office, which scholar-official opinion condemned.

sentences.zh: 至是以直言去，國人始稱焉。

translations.literal: By this time he left office for blunt speech, and his countrymen at last praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office for blunt speech, his countrymen at last praised him.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈官如弘緒。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given office like Hongxu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign he received the same posthumous honors as Hongxu.

sentences.zh: 懋遜，沾化人。

translations.literal: Maoxun was a native of Zhanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun came from Zhanhua.

sentences.zh: 為余姚知縣，有治績，入為吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yuyao with administrative achievements and entered office as supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Yuyao he governed well, then entered the capital as supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau.

sentences.zh: 既削籍，裏居三十年。

translations.literal: After being struck from the rolls, he lived at home thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: After being struck from the rolls, he lived at home for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起太仆少卿，累遷工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was raised to vice minister of the Imperial Stud and repeatedly promoted to left vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong came to the throne, he was recalled as vice minister of the Imperial Stud and rose to left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the office of minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as minister.

sentences.zh: 之佳，長洲人。

translations.literal: Zhijia was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijia came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為襄陽知縣。

translations.literal: At first he was magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as magistrate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 初春，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Chuchun was a native of Wu county.
translations.idiomatic: Chuchun came from Wu county.

sentences.zh: 初為順德知縣。

translations.literal: At first he was magistrate of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as magistrate of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 並以治行征。

translations.literal: Both were summoned for their administrative conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Both were summoned to the capital for their record of governance.

sentences.zh: 至是與張棟並斥，稱「吳中三諫」。

translations.literal: By this time they were dismissed together with Zhang Dong and were called "The Three Remonstrators of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: At this point they were dismissed along with Zhang Dong and became known as "The Three Remonstrators of Wu."

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈之佳太仆少卿，初春光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, Zhijia was posthumously given vice minister of the Imperial Stud and Chuchun vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign, Zhijia was posthumously honored as vice minister of the Imperial Stud and Chuchun as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 之佳孫適，亦兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Zhijia's grandson Shi also served as supervising secretary of the Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijia's grandson Shi also served as supervising secretary of the Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 敢言。

translations.literal: He spoke boldly.
translations.idiomatic: He was outspoken.

sentences.zh: 其休，青城人。

translations.literal: Qixiu was a native of Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qixiu came from Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 由蘇州推官擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: From investigating magistrate of Suzhou he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from investigating magistrate of Suzhou to supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau.

sentences.zh: 內官張德毆殺人，帝令司禮按問，蔽罪其下。

translations.literal: The inner eunuch Zhang De beat a man to death. The emperor ordered the Directorate of Ceremonial to investigate and concealed the crime by blaming subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Zhang De beat a man to death, the emperor ordered the Directorate of Ceremonial to investigate; it covered up the crime by blaming his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 其休乞並付德法司，竟報許。

translations.literal: Qixiu requested that De also be turned over to the judicial offices, and in the end the reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: Qixiu asked that De be handed over to the judicial authorities as well, and the request was eventually granted.

sentences.zh: 帝數不視朝。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly skipped court audiences.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，其休以萬邦入覲，請臨禦以風勵諸臣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year, Qixiu, on the occasion of tribute envoys from the ten thousand states coming to audience, requested that the emperor preside in person to inspire and encourage the officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wanli 17, with tributary envoys arriving for audience, Qixiu urged the emperor to preside in person and set an example for his officials.

sentences.zh: 他論奏甚眾。

translations.literal: His other memorials and proposals were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted many other memorials and proposals.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，卒，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: Dismissed and returned home, he died and was posthumously given vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After dismissal and retirement, he died and was posthumously honored as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嗣成，烏程人。

translations.literal: Sicheng was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng came from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 祖份，禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fen was minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fen had been minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父道醇，南京給事中。

translations.literal: His father Daochun was a supervising secretary in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daochun had been a supervising secretary in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 仍世貴顯。

translations.literal: For generations they were noble and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: The family had been eminent for generations.

sentences.zh: 嗣成以氣節著，士論多之。

translations.literal: Sicheng was noted for moral fortitude, and scholar opinion largely approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng was admired for his integrity, and scholar-official opinion largely favored him.

sentences.zh: 名儒，真定人。

translations.literal: Mingru was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Mingru came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 贈官如初春。

translations.literal: Posthumous office was given like Chuchun.
translations.idiomatic: He received the same posthumous honors as Chuchun.

sentences.zh: 棟，字伯任，昆山人。

translations.literal: Dong, style Boren, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dong, styled Boren, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 除新建知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 征授工科給事中。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed supervising secretary of the Works Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital and made supervising secretary of the Works Bureau.

sentences.zh: 請盡蠲天下逋租，格不行。

translations.literal: He requested that all back taxes nationwide be entirely remitted; the proposal was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He called for a full remission of all arrears in land tax nationwide, but the proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 時蠲租例，相沿但蠲存留，不及起運。

translations.literal: At that time the precedent for rent remission, handed down from custom, only remitted retained grain and did not extend to grain for transport.
translations.idiomatic: The prevailing precedent for rent remission covered only locally retained grain, not grain earmarked for transport.

sentences.zh: 棟請無拘故事，從之。

translations.literal: Dong requested not to be bound by precedent, and the request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong urged that precedent not be allowed to limit the remission, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to left supervising secretary of the Punishments Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left supervising secretary of the Punishments Bureau.

sentences.zh: 吳中白糧為累，民承役輒破家，棟請令出貲助漕舟附載。

translations.literal: White grain in Wu was burdensome; people undertaking corvée duty often ruined their households. Dong requested that they be allowed to pay money to help grain transport boats carry loads as supplementary freight.
translations.idiomatic: The white-grain levy in the Wu region ruined households pressed into transport duty. Dong proposed allowing taxpayers to pay a fee so their grain could ride aboard transport boats as supplementary cargo.

sentences.zh: 申時行、王錫爵絀其議，棟遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue blocked his proposal; Dong then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue blocked the proposal, and Dong retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 起兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was raised to chief supervising secretary of the Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as chief supervising secretary of the Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 劾去南京戶部尚書張西銘、刑部侍郎詹仰庇。

translations.literal: He impeached and brought down Zhang Ximing, minister of Revenue in Nanjing, and Zhan Yangbi, vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhang Ximing, Nanjing minister of Revenue, and Zhan Yangbi, vice minister of Punishments, out of office.

sentences.zh: 軍政拾遺，劾恭順侯吳繼爵、宣城伯衛國本、忻城伯趙泰修、宣府總兵官李迎恩。

translations.literal: In military administration he filled omissions; he impeached the marquis of Gongshun Wu Jijue, the earl of Xuancheng Wei Guoben, the earl of Xincheng Zhao Taixiu, and Li Ying'en, commander-in-chief of Xuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing military affairs, he impeached Marquis of Gongshun Wu Jijue, Earl of Xuancheng Wei Guoben, Earl of Xincheng Zhao Taixiu, and Xuanda commander Li Ying'en.

sentences.zh: 繼爵留，余並罷。

translations.literal: Jijue was retained; the rest were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jijue kept his post; the others were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 已，言邊臣敘功不宜及內閣、部、科，帝亦從焉。

translations.literal: Later he said that when border officials were recording merit, the Grand Secretariat, ministries, and bureaus ought not be included, and the emperor also followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Later he argued that frontier commanders awarding merit should not include the Grand Secretariat, ministries, or remonstrance bureaus, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遣視固原邊備。

translations.literal: He was sent to inspect border defenses at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to inspect the Guyuan frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 時經略鄭洛方議和，棟言撦力克負固不歸，卜失兔傑黠如故，火落赤、真相雄據海上，不可使洛委責以去。

translations.literal: At that time the frontier commissioner Zheng Luo was just then negotiating peace. Dong said Chelai still held obstinately and would not return, Buzhatu remained clever and crafty as before, and Huoluochi and Zhenxiang held the sea coast powerfully; Luo could not be allowed to leave by shifting responsibility onto others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luo was then negotiating peace. Dong warned that Chelai remained defiant, Buzhatu as cunning as ever, and Huoluochi and Zhenxiang still held the coast—that Luo must not be permitted to withdraw by passing off his duties.

sentences.zh: 因論兵部尚書王一鶚。

translations.literal: He thereby criticized Minister of War Wang Yihu.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to criticize Minister of War Wang Yihu.

sentences.zh: 會一鶚已卒，洛亦報撦力克東歸，遂寢其奏。

translations.literal: Just then Yihu had already died, and Luo also reported that Chelai had returned east; thus his memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yihu had already died, and Luo reported that Chelai had returned east, so the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 棟又言：「洮、河失事，陛下赫然震怒。

translations.literal: Dong also said: "The disaster on the Tao and He rivers—Your Majesty was suddenly and greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Dong added: "When the Tao-He frontier collapsed, Your Majesty was rightfully furious.

sentences.zh: 命洛視師，豈止欲其虛詞媚敵，博一順義東歸畢事耶？

translations.literal: You ordered Luo to oversee the army—is it only to want him to use empty words to flatter the enemy and gain one Shunyi's return east to finish the affair?"
translations.idiomatic: You sent Luo to take command—did you intend only that he flatter the enemy with empty phrases and declare victory when Shunyi returned east?"

sentences.zh: 今火、真依海為窟，出沒自如，不宜敘將吏功。

translations.literal: Now Huo and Zhen rely on the sea as a lair and come and go freely; it is not fitting to record merit for commanders and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluochi and Zhenxiang still use the coast as their base and raid at will; frontier officers should not be rewarded for merit now.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " The report was noted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 母卒，棟年已六十，毀瘠廬墓，竟卒於墓所。

translations.literal: His mother died. Dong was already sixty; emaciated from mourning he lived in a hut at the tomb and in the end died at the tomb site.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Dong, already sixty, grew gaunt with grief and lived in a mourning hut at her tomb, where he eventually died.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously honored as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 德泳，祭酒守益孫。

translations.literal: Deyong was the grandson of the libationer Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: Deyong was the grandson of the libationer Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 養浩、羽正自有傳。

translations.literal: Yanghao and Yuzheng have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yanghao and Yuzheng have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 孟養浩，字義甫，湖廣鹹寧人。

translations.literal: Meng Yanghao, style Yifu, was a native of Xianning in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yanghao, styled Yifu, came from Xianning in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 11.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier.

sentences.zh: 擢戶科給事中，遷左給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau and transferred to left supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau and then left supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝嚴譴李獻可，養浩疏諫曰：「人臣即至狂悖，未有敢於侮君者，陛下豈真以其侮而罪之耶？

translations.literal: The emperor severely rebuked Li Xianke. Yanghao remonstrated in a memorial, saying: "Even if a subject is utterly reckless, none dares insult the sovereign. Does Your Majesty truly punish him for insult?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor harshly punished Li Xianke, Yanghao memorialized in protest: "However reckless a subject may be, none would dare insult the throne. Does Your Majesty truly mean to punish him for lese-majeste?"

sentences.zh: 獻可甫躋禮垣，驟議巨典。

translations.literal: Xianke had just entered the Rites Bureau and suddenly debated a great state rite.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke had only just entered the Rites Bureau when he joined debate over a major state ceremony.

sentences.zh: 一字之誤，本屬無心，乃遽蒙顯斥。

translations.literal: A single character's error was in nature unintentional, yet he suddenly received conspicuous dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: A single mistaken character was plainly unintentional, yet he was swiftly and publicly punished.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為有五不可。

translations.literal: Your servant in foolishness believes there are five things that must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: I see five reasons this must not stand.

sentences.zh: 元子天下本，豫教之請，實為宗社計。

translations.literal: The primary son is the root of the realm; the request for early instruction is truly for the sake of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is the foundation of the realm. The call for his early instruction serves the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 陛下不惟不聽，且從而罰之，是坐忍元子失學，而敝帚宗社也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty not only did not listen but also punished accordingly—is this to sit by and allow the primary son to miss his schooling, and to treat the altars of state as a worn broom?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty not only refused but punished him—allowing the heir to go untaught and treating the dynasty like a worn-out broom."

sentences.zh: 不可者一。

translations.literal: The first thing that must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: First objection.

sentences.zh: 長幼定序，明旨森嚴，天下臣民既曉然諒陛下之無他矣。

translations.literal: Elder and younger have fixed order; the clear edict is sternly strict. Officials and people of the realm already understand clearly and trust that Your Majesty has no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: The order of succession is settled and Your Majesty's edicts are clear; the realm already trusts that you mean no other design.

sentences.zh: 然豫教、冊立？

translations.literal: Yet early instruction and formal investiture?
translations.idiomatic: Yet are early instruction and formal investiture—

sentences.zh: 本非兩事。

translations.literal: Originally they are not two matters.
translations.idiomatic: —not really separate matters?

sentences.zh: 今日既遲回於豫教，安知來歲不遊移於冊立，是重啟天下之疑。

translations.literal: Today you already hesitate over early instruction—who knows whether next year you will waver over formal investiture? This reopens the realm's doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Delay early instruction today, and who can say investiture will not be deferred next year? That would reopen doubts across the realm.

sentences.zh: 不可者二。

translations.literal: The second thing that must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Second objection.

sentences.zh: 父子之恩，根於天性，豫教之請，有益元子明甚。

translations.literal: The grace between father and son is rooted in natural feeling; the request for early instruction clearly benefits the primary son in the highest degree.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between father and son is natural, and early instruction plainly serves the heir.

sentences.zh: 而陛下罪之，非所以示慈愛。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty punishes it—this is not the way to display tender love.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing such a plea does not show fatherly kindness.

sentences.zh: 不可者三。

translations.literal: The third thing that must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Third objection.

sentences.zh: 古者引裾折檻之事，中主能容之。

translations.literal: In antiquity, cases of grasping the robe and breaking the railing—even mediocre rulers could tolerate them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity even mediocre rulers tolerated remonstrators who seized their robes or broke the balustrade.

sentences.zh: 陛下量侔天地，奈何言及宗社大計，反震怒而摧折之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's capacity equals heaven and earth—why, when speaking of great plans for the altars of state, do you instead flare in anger and break them?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's magnanimity matches heaven and earth—why rage and crush those who speak for the dynasty's welfare?

sentences.zh: 天下萬世謂陛下何如主？

translations.literal: What kind of ruler will the realm for ten thousand generations call Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: What will posterity think of such a ruler?

sentences.zh: 不可者四。

translations.literal: The fourth thing that must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth objection.

sentences.zh: 獻可等所論，非二三言官之私言，實天下臣民之公言也。

translations.literal: What Xianke and others discussed was not the private words of two or three remonstrating officials—it was truly the public words of officials and people of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke's plea was not the private opinion of a few censors but the voice of the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 今加罪獻可，是所罪者一人，而實失天下人之心。

translations.literal: Now if you add guilt to Xianke, the one punished is a single man, but in truth you lose the hearts of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing Xianke alone will alienate the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 不可者五。

translations.literal: The fifth thing that must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth objection.

sentences.zh: 祈陛下收還成命，亟行豫教。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty withdraw the completed order and swiftly carry out early instruction.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to revoke the sentence and proceed at once with early instruction.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，言冊立已諭於明年舉行，養浩疑君惑眾，殊可痛惡。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angry, saying formal investiture had already been announced for the next year, that Yanghao doubted the ruler and misled the masses, which was extremely painful and detestable.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious. Investiture, he said, was already scheduled for the next year. Yanghao, he charged, cast doubt on the throne and misled the people—a grievous offense.

sentences.zh: 令錦衣衛杖之百，削籍為民，永不敘用。

translations.literal: He ordered the Brocade Guard to beat him a hundred times, strike him from the rolls as a commoner, and never employ him again.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Brocade Guard to beat Yanghao a hundred strokes, strike him from the rolls, and bar him from office forever.

sentences.zh: 中外交薦，悉報寢。

translations.literal: Recommendations from within and without the court were all reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations from inside and outside court were all ignored.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was raised to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong came to the throne, he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 半歲中遷至南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Within half a year he was transferred to right vice minister of Punishments in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he was promoted to right vice minister of Punishments in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未之官，卒。

translations.literal: Before taking office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 朱維京，字大可，工部尚書衡子也。

translations.literal: Zhu Weijing, style Dake, was the son of Minister of Works Zhu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Weijing, styled Dake, was the son of Minister of Works Zhu Heng.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷五年進士，授大理評事，進右寺副。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli, was appointed review official of the Dali Court, and advanced to right vice director of the court.
translations.idiomatic: A Wanli 5 jinshi, he was appointed a Dali review official and rose to right vice director of the court.

sentences.zh: 九年京察，謫汝州同知，改知崇德。

translations.literal: In the ninth year's capital evaluation he was demoted to vice prefect of Ruzhou and transferred to magistrate of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli 9 capital evaluation he was demoted to vice prefect of Ruzhou, then reassigned as magistrate of Chongde.

sentences.zh: 入為屯田主事，再遷光祿丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director of field administration and was twice promoted to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he served as director of field administration and rose to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 火落赤敗盟，經略鄭洛主和，督撫魏學曾、葉夢熊主戰。

translations.literal: When Huoluochi broke the treaty, frontier commissioner Zheng Luo advocated peace while grand coordinators Wei Xuezeng and Ye Mengxiong advocated war.
translations.idiomatic: After Huoluochi broke the treaty, Commissioner Zheng Luo favored peace while Grand Coordinators Wei Xuezeng and Ye Mengxiong favored war.

sentences.zh: 維京請召洛還，專委學曾等經理。

translations.literal: Weijing requested that Luo be recalled and that management be entrusted solely to Xuezeng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Weijing urged Luo's recall and entrusted affairs exclusively to Xuezeng and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 及學曾以寧夏事被逮，復抗疏救之。

translations.literal: When Xuezeng was arrested over the Ningxia affair, he again submitted a bold memorial to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuezeng was arrested over the Ningxia affair, Weijing again memorialized boldly in his defense.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，三王並封詔下，維京首上疏曰：「往奉聖諭，許二十一年冊立，廷臣莫不延頸企踵。
