translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the edict enfeoffing the three princes together was issued, Weijing was first to memorialize, saying: "Formerly we received the sacred edict promising formal investiture in the twenty-first year; court officials all stretched their necks and stood on tiptoe in expectation."
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 21, when the edict enfeoffing all three princes was issued, Weijing was the first to memorialize: "Your Majesty's edict once promised investiture in Wanli 21. The entire court awaited it eagerly."

sentences.zh: 今忽改而為分封，是向者大號之頒，徒戲言也，何以示天下？

translations.literal: Now it is suddenly changed to separate enfeoffments—were the great proclamations of before merely playful words? How may this be shown to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Now enfeoffment replaces investiture—were your solemn promises mere jest? How can the realm trust your word?"

sentences.zh: 聖諭謂立嗣以嫡，是已。

translations.literal: The sacred edict said to establish the heir by the primary wife—so it was.
translations.idiomatic: Your edict held that the heir must be the eldest son of the empress—rightly so.

sentences.zh: 但元子既長，欲少遲冊立，以待中宮正嫡之生，則祖宗以來，實無此制。

translations.literal: But if the primary son is already grown and you wish to delay formal investiture slightly to await the birth of a legitimate son from the empress in the central palace—since the founding ancestors, there has truly been no such institution.
translations.idiomatic: If delay is meant to await a legitimate son from the empress, no such precedent exists since the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 考英宗之立，以宣德三年；

translations.literal: Consider Emperor Yingzong's investiture—in Xuande 3;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong was invested in Xuande 3;

sentences.zh: 憲宗之立，以正統十四年；

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong's investiture—in Zhengtong 14;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong in Zhengtong 14;

sentences.zh: 孝宗之立，以成化十一年。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong's investiture—in Chenghua 11.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong in Chenghua 11.

sentences.zh: 少者止一二齡，多亦不過五六齡耳。

translations.literal: The youngest were only one or two sui; at most they did not exceed five or six sui.
translations.idiomatic: None was older than five or six, and some were only one or two years old.

sentences.zh: 維時中宮正位，嫡嗣皆虛，而祖宗曾不少待。

translations.literal: At that time the empress occupied her proper place, yet legitimate heirs were all vacant—and the founding ancestors never waited even slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the empress sat in her rightful place and no legitimate son had yet been born, our ancestors never saw fit to delay.

sentences.zh: 即陛下冊立，亦在先帝二年之春。

translations.literal: Even Your Majesty's own investiture as heir occurred in the spring of the second year of the late emperor's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was yourself invested in the spring of your father's second year on the throne.

sentences.zh: 近事不遠，何不取而證之。

translations.literal: Recent events are not far removed—why not take them as proof?
translations.idiomatic: That precedent is close at hand; why not hold it up as evidence?

sentences.zh: 且聖人為政，必先正名。

translations.literal: Moreover, when sages govern, they must first set names aright.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's way of governance begins with rectifying names and ranks.

sentences.zh: 今分封之典，三王並舉，冠服宮室混而無別，車馬儀仗雜而無章，府僚庶寀淆而無辨。

translations.literal: Now in the rite of enfeoffment, three princes are elevated together; caps and robes and palace quarters are mingled without distinction; chariots, horses, and ceremonial regalia are mixed without proper order; palace staff and stipends are confused without differentiation.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes are to be enfeoffed at once, with no distinction in dress, palaces, equipage, retinues, or stipends.

sentences.zh: 名既不正，弊實滋多。

translations.literal: When names are not set aright, abuses in fact will multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Once titles and ranks are blurred, mischief quickly follows.

sentences.zh: 且令中宮茍耀前星，則元子退就藩服，嫡庶分定，何嫌何疑。

translations.literal: Moreover, if the empress should one day bring brilliance to the Heir Apparent Star, then the primary son would withdraw to his fief and robe of rank; legitimate and secondary lines would be fixed—what suspicion or doubt would remain?
translations.idiomatic: If the empress later bears a son, the eldest prince can take up his fief while succession is settled—where is the difficulty?

sentences.zh: 今預計將來，坐格成命，是欲愚天下，而實以天下為戲也。

translations.literal: Now you plan for the future in advance and let a fixed decree stand—this is wishing to deceive all under Heaven, and in truth treating the realm as a game.
translations.idiomatic: To prejudge the future and lock in this decree is to mock the realm and treat the throne like sport.

sentences.zh: 夫人臣以道事君，不可則止。

translations.literal: A minister serves his ruler by the Way; if it cannot be done, he stops.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister serves by principle and, when overruled, knows when to stand down.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖有並封之意，猶不遽行，必以手詔咨大學士王錫爵，錫爵縱不能如李沆引燭之焚，亦當為李泌造膝披陳，轉移聖心而後已。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has the intention of joint enfeoffment, you have not yet hastened to carry it out and must consult Grand Secretary Wang Xijue by personal edict; even if Xijue cannot emulate Li Hang burning an edict by candlelight, he ought at least to follow Li Bi in kneeling close to speak forthrightly, and not desist until he has turned the sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: You still consulted Wang Xijue by private edict before acting—he might not burn the decree as Li Hang did, but he should have pleaded face to face like Li Bi until your mind was changed.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，王家屏之高蹤自在，陛下優禮輔臣，必無韓瑗、來濟之辱也。

translations.literal: If that were not so, Wang Jiaping's lofty path of withdrawal lies open; Your Majesty treats chief ministers with honor—there would surely be none of the disgrace suffered by Han Yuan and Lai Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Failing that, he could follow Wang Jiaping's example and withdraw; under your generous treatment of ministers, he would not share Han Yuan and Lai Ji's fate.

sentences.zh: 奈何噤無一語，若胥吏之承行，惟恐或後。

translations.literal: Yet how is it that he holds his tongue without a single word, like a clerk receiving orders for execution, afraid only of being late?
translations.idiomatic: Instead he said nothing, hurrying the order through like a clerk afraid of falling behind.

sentences.zh: 彼楊素、李勣千古罪人，其初心豈不知有公論，惟是患得患失之心勝，遂至不能自持耳。

translations.literal: Those men Yang Su and Li Ji are sinners through the ages; at the outset did they not know there was public opinion? Only the heart of fretting over loss and gain prevailed, until they could no longer hold themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and Li Ji are condemned by history; they knew better, but fear of losing favor overcame conscience.

sentences.zh: 」帝震怒，命謫戍極邊。

translations.literal: 」 The emperor was shaken with rage and ordered him banished to guard the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered exile to the remotest border.

sentences.zh: 錫爵力救，得為民。

translations.literal: Xijue vigorously interceded, and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue pleaded forcefully on his behalf, and the sentence was commuted to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 家居甫二年，卒。

translations.literal: At home only two years, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years into retirement, he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianqi he was posthumously given the title Vice Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 王如堅，字介石，安福人。

translations.literal: Wang Rujian, styled Jieshi, a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rujian (Jieshi), from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 14.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 14.

sentences.zh: 授懷慶推官。

translations.literal: Appointed investigating censor of Huaqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed legal officer of Huaqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為刑科給事中，抗疏爭三王並封，其略曰：

translations.literal: Entered service as supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments, remonstrating by memorial against the three princes' joint enfeoffment; the substance said:
translations.idiomatic: Later promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments, he submitted a forceful memorial against enfeoffing all three princes. It read, in part:

sentences.zh: 謹按十四年正月聖諭「元子幼小，冊立事俟二三年舉行」，是明言長子之為元子也。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering the holy instruction of the first month of year fourteen: "The primary son is young; the matter of investiture shall await two or three years"—this clearly states that the eldest son is the primary son.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 14 you declared that the eldest son was still young and investiture would wait two or three years—a plain acknowledgment that he was heir.

sentences.zh: 又十八年正月詔旨「朕無嫡子，長幼自有定序」，是明示倫次之不可易也。

translations.literal: Again, the edict of the first month of year eighteen: "I have no legitimate son; seniority and juniority have their fixed order"—this clearly shows that the moral order cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen you said that without a legitimate son, birth order still fixed succession—an unmistakable pledge that rank could not be overturned.

sentences.zh: 已而十九年八月，奉旨「冊立之事，改於二十一年舉行」，此則陛下雖怒群臣激聒，輒更定期，未嘗遽寢冊立之事。

translations.literal: Then in the eighth month of year nineteen, receiving the decree: "The matter of investiture is changed to be conducted in year twenty-one"—here, though Your Majesty was angry at the ministers' clamor and repeatedly changed the date, you never hastily abandoned the matter of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: When court debate grew heated you pushed the date to year twenty-one—but you never abandoned investiture itself.

sentences.zh: 乃今已屆期，忽傳並封為王，以待嫡嗣。

translations.literal: Yet now the deadline has arrived, and suddenly word comes of joint enfeoffment as kings, to await a legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with the deadline reached, you suddenly propose to enfeoff all three as princes while waiting for a legitimate son.

sentences.zh: 臣始而疑，既而駭。

translations.literal: Your servant at first doubted, then was appalled.
translations.idiomatic: At first I doubted my ears; then I was stunned.

sentences.zh: 陛下言猶在耳，豈忘之耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's words still ring in the ears—have you forgotten them?
translations.idiomatic: Your own words still ring in our ears—have you forgotten them?

sentences.zh: 曩者謂二三年舉行，已遲至二十年矣，二十年舉行又改至二十一年矣，今二十一年倏改為並封，是陛下前此灼然之命，尚不自堅，今日群臣，將何所取信？

translations.literal: Formerly it was said to be conducted in two or three years—it was already delayed until year twenty; conduct in year twenty was again changed to year twenty-one; now in year twenty-one it is suddenly changed to joint enfeoffment—if Your Majesty's clearly stated commands of before are not even held firm by yourself, how are the ministers of today to find anything to trust?
translations.idiomatic: "Two or three years" became twenty, then twenty-one—and now joint enfeoffment. If even you will not stand by your own decrees, how can your ministers trust anything you say?

sentences.zh: 夫立嫡之條，《祖訓》為廢嫡者戒也。

translations.literal: As for the rule of establishing the legitimate heir, the Ancestral Instructions warn those who would depose the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: The rule of legitimate succession is enshrined in the Ancestral Instructions as a warning against displacing the heir.

sentences.zh: 今日有嫡可廢乎？

translations.literal: Today is there a legitimate heir who can be deposed?
translations.idiomatic: Is there now a legitimate heir whom you mean to set aside?

sentences.zh: 且陛下欲待正嫡，意非真待也。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Your Majesty wishes to await a proper legitimate son, the intention is not truly to wait.
translations.idiomatic: And this professed wait for a legitimate son from the empress is not sincere.

sentences.zh: 古王者後宮無偏愛，故適後多後嗣。

translations.literal: Ancient kings had no partiality in the inner palaces, hence the principal consorts often bore many heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings did not favor one consort above others, so empresses often bore many sons.

sentences.zh: 後世愛有所專，則天地之交不常泰，欲後嗣之繁難矣。

translations.literal: In later ages when love has a single focus, then the union of Heaven and Earth is not constantly peaceful, and to desire abundant heirs becomes difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's affection settles on one woman alone, Heaven's favor wanes and heirs grow scarce.

sentences.zh: 我祖宗以來，中宮誕生者有幾？

translations.literal: Since our founding ancestors, how many sons have been born from the empress?
translations.idiomatic: How often, since the dynasty was founded, has an empress actually borne a son?

sentences.zh: 國本早定，惟元子是屬。

translations.literal: The foundation of the state was early fixed; only the primary son was destined for it.
translations.idiomatic: The succession was always settled early upon the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 或二三齡而立，或五六齡而立。

translations.literal: Some were invested at two or three sui, some at five or six sui.
translations.idiomatic: Some heirs were invested at two or three years, others at five or six.

sentences.zh: 即陛下春宮受冊時，止六齡耳，寧有待嫡之議與潞王並封之詔哉？

translations.literal: Even when Your Majesty received investiture in the Eastern Palace, you were only six sui—was there ever talk of waiting for a legitimate son or an edict jointly enfeoffing the Prince of Lu?
translations.idiomatic: You yourself were invested at six—was there ever talk of waiting for a legitimate son, or of enfeoffing the Prince of Lu alongside you?

sentences.zh: 今皇長子且十二齡矣，聞皇后撫育無間己出。

translations.literal: Now the eldest imperial son is already twelve sui; I hear the empress has reared him without difference from her own issue.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest prince is already twelve, and the empress has raised him as if he were her own.

sentences.zh: 元子早定一日，即早慰中宮一日之心。

translations.literal: If the primary son is fixed one day earlier, that is one day earlier in comforting the empress's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Confirming the heir one day sooner would bring the empress one day of peace.

sentences.zh: 後素賢明，何有舍當前之冢嗣，而覬幸不可知之數耶？

translations.literal: The empress has always been wise and clear-sighted—how could she abandon the present heir and covet the uncertain reckoning of chance?
translations.idiomatic: The empress is wise—why would she forsake a ready heir for some uncertain future?

sentences.zh: 宮闈之內，衽席之間，左右近習之輩，見形生疑，未必不以他意窺陛下。

translations.literal: Within the inner palaces, between bed and mat, the attendants close at hand—seeing how matters stand, suspicion arises; they may not fail to probe Your Majesty with other intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace, those nearest you will read every gesture for hidden meaning.

sentences.zh: 即如昨歲冊立之旨，方待舉行，而宗室中已有並封之疏，安知非機事外泄，彼得量朝廷之淺深？

translations.literal: Take, for example, last year's investiture decree, which was still awaiting execution—yet within the imperial clan there were already memorials on joint enfeoffment; who knows whether confidential affairs were not leaked abroad, so that they could gauge the depth or shallowness of the court?
translations.idiomatic: Last year's investiture edict had not yet been carried out when clansmen were already petitioning for joint enfeoffment—had state secrets leaked so they could test the court's resolve?

sentences.zh: 夫別名號，辨嫌疑，禮之善經也。

translations.literal: To distinguish titles and names and clarify suspicion is a fine constant of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Distinguishing titles to dispel suspicion is one of ritual's deepest purposes.

sentences.zh: 元子與眾子，其間冠服之制，齒簿之節，恩寵之數，接見之儀，迥然不齊矣。

translations.literal: Between the primary son and the other sons, the systems of cap and robe, the protocols of age and registry, the measure of favor, and the ceremonies of audience are strikingly unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Between heir and younger sons, dress, protocol, favor, and audience rights are sharply different by design.

sentences.zh: 一日並封而同號，則有並大之嫌，逼長之患。

translations.literal: In one day jointly enfeoffing them with the same title—then there is the suspicion of shared primacy and the peril of pressing against the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing them together under one title invites rivalry with the heir and disrespect for seniority.

sentences.zh: 執狐疑而來讒賊，幾微之際，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Holding to doubt brings slanderers; at the subtle turning point, one cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Ambiguity invites intrigue; at such a delicate moment, caution is everything.

sentences.zh: 茍謂渙命新頒，難於遽改，則數年已定之明旨，尚可移易，今綸言初發，何不可中止也。

translations.literal: If one says a newly issued edict is hard to change hastily—then clear decrees fixed for years could still be altered; now that the imperial words have only just been issued, why can they not be halted?
translations.idiomatic: If a fresh edict cannot be reversed, how were your earlier promises so easily changed? This decree has barely been issued—it can still be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，命與朱維京皆戍極邊。

translations.literal: The emperor was extremely angry and ordered both him and Zhu Weijing banished to guard the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor ordered both Wang Rujian and Zhu Weijing exiled to the remote frontier.

sentences.zh: 王錫爵疏救，免戍為民。

translations.literal: Wang Xijue submitted a memorial to rescue them; banishment was remitted and they were made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue interceded, and their exile was commuted to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he was posthumously honored as Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 王學曾，字唯吾，南海人。

translations.literal: Wang Xuezeng, styled Weiwo, a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuezeng (Weiwo), from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 5.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 授醴陵知縣，調崇陽。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Liling, then transferred to Chongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Liling, then was transferred to Chongyang.

sentences.zh: 擢南京御史。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 時吏民有罪，輒遣官校逮捕。

translations.literal: At the time, when officials or commoners had committed offences, palace guards were always dispatched to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, offenders among officials and commoners were routinely seized by palace guards.

sentences.zh: 學曾疏請止之，不納。

translations.literal: Xuezeng submitted a memorial requesting this be stopped; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuezeng memorialized to halt the practice, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 十三年，慈寧宮成，諸督工內侍俱蔭錦衣。

translations.literal: In year thirteen, when Cining Palace was completed, all the eunuchs supervising the work were granted hereditary appointments in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 13, when Cining Palace was finished, every supervising eunuch received hereditary rank in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 學曾論其太濫，且劾工部尚書楊兆諛諂中官。

translations.literal: Xuezeng argued the awards were too excessive, and also impeached Minister of Works Yang Zhao for flattering the inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuezeng denounced the rewards as excessive and impeached Works Minister Yang Zhao for toadying to eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 兆惶恐，引罪。

translations.literal: Zhao was fearful and acknowledged his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao, alarmed, confessed his fault.

sentences.zh: 已，言龍江關密邇蕪湖，蕪湖已征稅，龍江不宜復征，格不行。

translations.literal: Later, he stated that Longjiang Pass lies close to Wuhu; since Wuhu already levies taxes, Longjiang ought not be taxed again—the proposal was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Longjiang Pass, so near taxed Wuhu, should not be levied again; the proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 光山牛產一犢若麟，有司欲以聞，巡撫臧惟一不可。

translations.literal: At Guangshan a cow bore a calf resembling a qilin; the local authorities wished to report it, but Grand Coordinator Zang Weiyi refused.
translations.idiomatic: When a cow at Guangshan bore a qilin-like calf, officials sought to report it, but Grand Coordinator Zang Weiyi refused.

sentences.zh: 帝命禮部征之，尚書沈鯉諫，惟一亦疏論，不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to summon it; Minister Shen Li remonstrated, and Weiyi also submitted a memorial arguing against it—the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to fetch the beast; Minister Shen Li objected, and Zang Weiyi memorialized too, all in vain.

sentences.zh: 學曾抗言：「麟生牛腹，次日即斃，則祥者已不祥矣。

translations.literal: Xuezeng remonstrated forcefully: "The qilin born from a cow's belly died the next day—then what was auspicious was already inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuezeng protested: "A qilin born from a cow died the next day—whatever omen it seemed was already null.

sentences.zh: 不祥之物，所司未嘗上聞，陛下何自聞之？

translations.literal: An inauspicious object—the responsible offices never reported it upward; how did Your Majesty hear of it yourself?
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities never reported this ill omen—so how did it reach your ears?

sentences.zh: 毋亦左右小人以奇怪惑聖心也？

translations.literal: Is it not rather that petty men at your side use strangeness to bewilder the sage heart?
translations.idiomatic: Surely petty attendants are using portents to sway your judgment?

sentences.zh: 今四方災旱，老稚流離，啼饑號寒之聲，陛下不聞；

translations.literal: Now throughout the four directions are calamity and drought; old and young wander destitute—the sounds of weeping from hunger and crying from cold Your Majesty does not hear;
translations.idiomatic: Famine and drought wrack the realm; the cries of starving refugees never reach you;

sentences.zh: 北敵梟張，士卒困苦，呻吟嗟怨之狀，陛下不聞；

translations.literal: Northern enemies are savagely rampant; soldiers suffer hardship—the spectacle of groaning and sighing in resentment Your Majesty does not hear;
translations.idiomatic: Enemies harry the northern frontier while wounded soldiers groan unheard;

sentences.zh: 宗室貧窮，饔餐弗給，愁困涕洟之態，陛下不聞；

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen are poor; meals are not provided—the appearance of grief, distress, tears, and mucus Your Majesty does not hear;
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished clansmen go hungry, their misery and tears unnoticed;

sentences.zh: 而獨已斃之麟聞。

translations.literal: Yet alone the already dead qilin is heard.
translations.idiomatic: yet word of a dead qilin somehow reaches your throne.

sentences.zh: 彼為左右者，豈誠忠於陛下乎？

translations.literal: Those who attend you—are they truly loyal to Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Are those at your side truly loyal to you?

sentences.zh: 願收還成命，內臣語涉邪妄者，即嚴斥之。

translations.literal: I wish you would recall the finalized decree; inner eunuchs whose words touch upon heterodox absurdity—immediately sternly rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw the order, and punish any eunuch who traffics in such superstition.

sentences.zh: 」帝責其要名沽直，降興國判官。

translations.literal: 」 The emperor reproached him for seeking fame and trading on integrity, and demoted him to judge of Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of grandstanding and demoted him to magistrate of Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 時御史蔡時鼎亦以言獲罪。

translations.literal: At the time Supervising Censor Cai Shiding was also punished for his words.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cai Shiding was punished at the same time for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 南京御史王藩臣、給事中王嗣美等交章救兩人。

translations.literal: Nanjing Censor Wang Fanchen, Supervising Secretary Wang Simei, and others submitted successive memorials to rescue the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Censor Wang Fanchen, Supervising Secretary Wang Simei, and others jointly memorialized in their defense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪俸一級。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and docked them one grade of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered, cut their salaries by one grade.

sentences.zh: 學曾累遷南京刑部主事，召為光祿丞。

translations.literal: Xuezeng was repeatedly promoted to principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, then summoned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuezeng rose to principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and was then recalled as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 與少卿涂傑合疏爭三王並封，忤旨，皆削籍。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Director Tu Jie he jointly memorialized against the three princes' joint enfeoffment; defying the imperial will, both were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He and Vice Director Tu Jie jointly opposed the three-prince enfeoffment; offending the throne, both were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後數年，吏部尚書蔡國珍疏請起用，不納。

translations.literal: Several years later, Minister of Personnel Cai Guozhen submitted a memorial requesting their reappointment—it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Personnel Minister Cai Guozhen recommended their reinstatement, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died in retirement at his home.

sentences.zh: 傑，新建人。

translations.literal: Jie was a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Jie was from Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Longqing 5.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Longqing 5.

sentences.zh: 由龍遊知縣入為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Longyou he entered service as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Censorate after serving as magistrate of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 擢官光祿。

translations.literal: Promoted to an office in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，贈學曾太仆少卿，傑太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the Xizong reign, Xuezeng was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and Jie Vice Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, Xuezeng was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and Jie Vice Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 張貞觀，字惟誠，沛人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhenguan, styled Weicheng, a native of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan (Weicheng), from Pei.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 11.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Wanli 11.

sentences.zh: 除益都知縣，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Yidu, promoted supervising secretary of the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yidu, then promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 出閱山西邊務。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect border affairs in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to inspect Shanxi frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 五臺奸人張守清招亡命三千余人，擅開銀礦，又締姻潞城、新寧二王。

translations.literal: At Wutai the villain Zhang Shouqing gathered more than three thousand fugitives, opened silver mines on his own authority, and also formed marriage alliances with the Princes of Lucheng and Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: At Wutai, Zhang Shouqing recruited three thousand outlaws, seized silver mines illegally, and allied himself by marriage with the Princes of Lucheng and Xinning.

sentences.zh: 帝納巡按御史言，敕守清解散徒黨，諭二王絕姻。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted the touring censor's report and ordered Shouqing to disband his band, instructing the two princes to sever the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on the touring censor's report, the emperor ordered Zhang to disband his followers and told both princes to break the alliance.

sentences.zh: 守清乞輸課於官，開礦如故。

translations.literal: Shouqing begged to pay levies to the government and continue opening mines as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shouqing offered to pay taxes to the state if mining could continue.

sentences.zh: 貞觀力爭，乃已。

translations.literal: Zhenguan vigorously contended, and only then was it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan fought the proposal until it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫沈子木、李采菲皆貪。

translations.literal: The former grand coordinators Shen Zimu and Li Caifei were both corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Former grand coordinators Shen Zimu and Li Caifei had both been corrupt.

sentences.zh: 子木夤緣為兵部侍郎，貞觀並追劾之。

translations.literal: Zimu had curried favor to become vice minister of war; Zhenguan also pursued impeachment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zimu had recently risen to vice minister of war through pull; Zhang Zhenguan impeached him as well.

sentences.zh: 子木坐貶，采菲奪職。

translations.literal: Zimu sat in judgement and was demoted; Caifei was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zimu was demoted and Li Caifei dismissed.

sentences.zh: 還，進工科右給事中。

translations.literal: Upon return, promoted to right supervising secretary of the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made right supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 泗州淮水大溢，幾嚙祖陵。

translations.literal: At Sizhou the Huai River greatly overflowed, nearly gnawing at the ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai flooded at Sizhou, it nearly reached the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀往視，定分黃道淮之策。

translations.literal: Zhenguan went to inspect and settled on the strategy of dividing the Yellow River channel from the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan inspected the disaster and devised the plan to divert the Yellow River away from the Huai.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: Again promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三王並封制下，貞觀率同列力爭。

translations.literal: When the edict enfeoffing the three princes jointly was issued, Zhenguan led his colleagues in vigorously protesting.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict to enfeoff all three princes at once was promulgated, Zhang Zhenguan led his colleagues in forceful opposition.

sentences.zh: 沈王呈堯由郡王進封，其諸弟止應為將軍，呈堯為營得郡王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shen, Chengyao, was promoted from prince of a commandery; his younger brothers should only have been made generals, but Chengyao lobbied and obtained the rank of commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shen, Chengyao, had been advanced from commandery prince, whereas his younger brothers were entitled only to the rank of general—yet Chengyao campaigned until he secured a commandery princedom for himself.

sentences.zh: 貞觀及禮部尚書羅萬化守故事極諫。

translations.literal: Zhenguan and Minister of Rites Luo Wanhua, adhering to precedent, remonstrated to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan and Minister of Rites Luo Wanhua remonstrated vigorously, insisting on the authority of established precedent.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not accept [it].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時郊廟祭享率遣官代行，貞觀力請帝親祀。

translations.literal: At the time suburban and temple sacrifices were routinely performed by dispatched officials as proxies; Zhenguan earnestly requested that the emperor perform the rites in person.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples were routinely delegated to officials, but Zhang Zhenguan pressed hard for the emperor to officiate in person.

sentences.zh: 俄秋享，復將遣官。

translations.literal: Soon, for the autumn offering, officials were again to be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when the autumn sacrifice came round, officials were once again to be sent in the emperor's stead.

sentences.zh: 貞觀再諫，不報。

translations.literal: Zhenguan remonstrated again; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan remonstrated again, to no reply.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，有詔皇長子出閣講讀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, an edict ordered the eldest imperial son to leave the inner quarters and commence lecturing and study.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, an edict called for the crown prince to leave the inner palace and begin his formal study under tutors.

sentences.zh: 而兵部請護衛，工部奏儀仗，禮部進儀註，皆留中。

translations.literal: But the Ministry of War requested guards of honor, the Ministry of Works submitted ceremonial insignia, and the Ministry of Rites advanced ritual protocols—all held back in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War petitioned for an escort, the Ministry of Works submitted plans for ceremonial regalia, and the Ministry of Rites presented ritual protocols—all held back in the palace with no decision.

sentences.zh: 又止令預告奉先殿，朝謁兩宮，他禮皆廢。

translations.literal: Moreover, it was only ordered to announce beforehand at the Hall of Ancestral Offerings and pay court to the two palaces; all other rites were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the heir was merely to announce his departure at the Hall of Ancestral Offerings and pay court to the empress dowagers—all other ceremonies were set aside.

sentences.zh: 於是貞觀等上言：「禮官議，禦門受賀、皇長子見群臣之禮，載在舊儀；

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhenguan and others submitted a memorial: "The ritual officials have determined that the rites of receiving congratulations at the Imperial Gate and the eldest imperial son's audience with the officials and ministers are recorded in the old regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan and his colleagues submitted a memorial: "The ritual officials have established that the ceremonies for receiving congratulations at the Imperial Gate and for the crown prince's audience with officials and ministers are set forth in the established regulations;

sentences.zh: 即諸王加冠，亦以成禮而賀，賀畢謁見。

translations.literal: Even when princes receive the capping ceremony, they likewise complete the rites and receive congratulations, and after congratulations pay their respects in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Even when lesser princes undergo the capping ceremony, they complete the full rites, receive congratulations, and thereafter pay their respects in audience.

sentences.zh: 元子初出，乃不當諸王一冠乎？

translations.literal: When the eldest son first leaves [the inner quarters], should he not [receive rites] equal to a prince's capping?
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent first leaves the inner palace, should he not receive ceremonies comparable to a prince's capping?

sentences.zh: 且謁謝止兩宮，而缺然於陛下及中宮母妃之前，非所以教孝；

translations.literal: Moreover, paying respects is limited to the two palaces, yet absent before Your Majesty and the empress and concubine mothers—is this how to teach filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: And to limit expressions of gratitude to the two palaces while omitting them before Your Majesty and the empress and imperial consorts—is this how one teaches filial devotion?

sentences.zh: 賀靳於二皇子，而漠然於兄弟長幼之間，非所以序別。

translations.literal: Congratulations are granted to the two princes, yet indifference toward the order of seniority among brothers—is this how to teach distinction in rank?
translations.idiomatic: To restrict congratulations to the two princes while showing indifference to the order of elder and younger among brothers—is this how one teaches proper rank and precedence?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，忤旨，奪俸一年。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it offended the imperial will; salary was withheld for one year.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, it gave offense; Zhang Zhenguan's salary was suspended for a year.

sentences.zh: 工科給事中黎道照上言：「元子初就外傅，陛下宜示之身教。

translations.literal: Li Daozhao, supervising secretary of the Bureau of Works, submitted a memorial: "When the eldest son first receives an outside tutor, Your Majesty ought to teach him by personal example.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daozhao, supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works, submitted a memorial: "When the heir first takes an outside tutor, Your Majesty should teach him by example.

sentences.zh: 乃采辦珠玉珍寶，費至三十六萬有奇，又取太仆銀十萬充賞，非作法於初之意。

translations.literal: Yet pearls, jade, and precious treasures were procured, costing more than 360,000; furthermore 100,000 taels of silver from the Court of the Imperial Stud were taken as rewards—this is not the intention of setting an example at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pearls, jade, and other precious goods were procured at a cost of more than 360,000 taels, and 100,000 taels from the Imperial Stud were drawn for rewards—hardly the spirit of setting a moral example at the outset.

sentences.zh: 且貞觀等秉禮直諫，職也，不宜罰治。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhenguan and others, upholding rites in direct remonstrance, were discharging their duty; they should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in speaking plainly in defense of ritual, Zhang Zhenguan and his colleagues were only doing their duty—they should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 」給事中趙完璧等亦言之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Zhao Wanbi and others also spoke to this effect.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Zhao Wanbi and others raised the same objections.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪諸臣俸，謫貞觀雜職。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, stripped the officials of their salaries, and demoted Zhenguan to a miscellaneous appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, suspended the salaries of all involved, and demoted Zhang Zhenguan to a minor post.

sentences.zh: 大學士王錫爵等切救，乃貶三秩。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Wang Xijue and others urgently pleaded for him; he was finally demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Wang Xijue and others pleaded urgently on his behalf, and the punishment was reduced to a demotion of three ranks.

sentences.zh: 頃之，都給事中許弘綱、御史陳惟芝等連章申論，帝竟除貞觀名，言官亦停俸。

translations.literal: Before long, Chief Supervising Secretary Xu Honggang, Censor Chen Weizhi, and others submitted successive memorials arguing the case; the emperor finally removed Zhenguan from the roster, and the remonstrating officials also had their salaries suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chief Supervising Secretary Xu Honggang, Censor Chen Weizhi, and others submitted a series of memorials in his defense. The emperor went so far as to strike Zhang Zhenguan's name from the rolls, and the remonstrating officials likewise had their salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 中外交薦，卒不起。

translations.literal: Officials inside and outside the court recommended him, but in the end he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended repeatedly by officials inside and outside the court, but never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 天啟中卒，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: He died during the Tianqi reign and was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Tianqi reign and was posthumously made Vice Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 樊玉衡，字以齊，黃岡人。

translations.literal: Fan Yuheng, styled Yiji, a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuheng (Yiji), from Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 11.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Wanli 11.

sentences.zh: 由廣信推官征授御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate-assessor of Guangxin he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Censorate after serving as magistrate-assessor in Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 京察，謫無為判官。

translations.literal: In the capital evaluation, he was demoted to judge of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital evaluation of officials, he was demoted to judge of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 稍遷全椒知縣。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to magistrate of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to magistrate of Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 二十六年四月，玉衡以冊立久稽，上言：「陛下愛貴妃，當圖所以善處之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Wanli 26, Yuheng, because investiture of the heir had long been delayed, submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty loves the Noble Consort and ought to devise a way to treat her well.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Wanli 26, Fan Yuheng, noting how long the heir's investiture had been delayed, submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty loves the Noble Consort and should find a way to treat her properly.

sentences.zh: 今天下無不以冊立之稽歸過貴妃者，而陛下又故依違，以成其過。

translations.literal: Today everyone under heaven blames the Noble Consort for the delay in investiture, yet Your Majesty deliberately wavers, thereby completing her fault.
translations.idiomatic: Today the whole realm blames the Noble Consort for the delay in investiture, yet Your Majesty deliberately vacillates, thereby making her the scapegoat.

sentences.zh: 陛下將何以托貴妃於天下哉？

translations.literal: How will Your Majesty entrust the Noble Consort to all under heaven?
translations.idiomatic: How will Your Majesty answer to the realm on the Noble Consort's behalf?

sentences.zh: 由元子而觀則不慈，由貴妃而觀則不智，無一可者。

translations.literal: Viewed from the eldest son, it is unkind; viewed from the Noble Consort, it is unwise—nothing in it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: From the heir's perspective it shows a lack of kindness; from the Noble Consort's, a lack of wisdom—there is nothing defensible in it.

sentences.zh: 願早定大計，冊立、冠婚諸典次第舉行，使天下以元子之安為貴妃功，豈不並受其福，享令名無窮哉！

translations.literal: I pray that the great plan be settled early, that the rites of investiture, capping, and marriage be carried out in turn, so that all under heaven may regard the eldest son's security as the Noble Consort's achievement—would they not together enjoy its blessings and an endless good name!
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty settle this great matter at once, and carry out investiture, capping, and marriage in due order, so that the realm may credit the heir's security to the Noble Consort's merit—would they not share the blessing and win an enduring good name together!

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，帝及貴妃怒甚。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor and the Noble Consort were exceedingly angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor and the Noble Consort were furious.

sentences.zh: 旨一日三四擬，禍且不測。

translations.literal: Imperial rescripts were drafted three or four times in a single day; disaster was incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial rescripts ordering punishment were drafted three or four times in a single day; his fate hung in the balance.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯等力救，言自帝即位未嘗殺諫臣。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and others vigorously pleaded for him, saying that since the emperor's accession he had never executed a remonstrating official.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and others pleaded vigorously on his behalf, reminding the emperor that since his accession no remonstrating official had ever been put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝乃焚其疏，忍而不發。

translations.literal: The emperor then burned his memorial and restrained himself from acting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor burned the memorial and held his anger in check.

sentences.zh: 再逾月，以《憂危竑議》連及，遂永戍雷州。

translations.literal: After another month, implicated through the Admonitions in Peril, he was permanently exiled to Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Another month later, implicated in the affair of the Admonitions in Peril, he was permanently banished to Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 長子鼎遇伏闕請代者再，不許。

translations.literal: His eldest son Dingyu twice prostrated himself at the palace gate to request taking his father's place; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Dingyu twice knelt at the palace gate begging to take his father's place in exile, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起南京刑部主事，以老辭。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended the throne, he was recalled as secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice but declined on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Fan Yuheng was recalled as secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice but declined on account of his age.

sentences.zh: 疏陳親賢、遠奸十事，優詔答之。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth ten matters on honoring the worthy and keeping the wicked at a distance; an edict of praise replied to him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial outlining ten measures for honoring the worthy and distancing the wicked, and received a gracious edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 尋命以太常少卿致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to retire as Vice Minister of Ceremonial and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted retirement as Vice Minister of Ceremonial and died at home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，遷戶部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, he was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 歷泉州知府、福建副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Quanzhou and vice commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Quanzhou and then as vice commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 八年，以大計罷歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was dismissed and returned home in the grand evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was dismissed in the grand evaluation of officials and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十六年，黃州城南門哭五日夜。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, [people] wept at the south gate of Huangzhou city for five days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, mourners wailed at the south gate of Huangzhou for five days and nights.

sentences.zh: 眾知禍必至，傾城走，婦女多不及行。

translations.literal: The people knew disaster was sure to come; the whole city fled, and many women could not get away in time.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing disaster was imminent, the whole city fled; many women could not escape in time.

sentences.zh: 三月二十四日，張獻忠破黃岡，知縣孫自一、縣丞吳文燮死之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, Zhang Xianzhong captured Huanggang; Magistrate Sun Ziyi and Assistant Magistrate Wu Wenxie died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, Zhang Xianzhong took Huanggang; Magistrate Sun Ziyi and Assistant Magistrate Wu Wenxie died defending the city.

sentences.zh: 賊欲屈維城，抗聲大罵，刃洞胸而死。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to break Weicheng; he shouted curses in a loud voice and died with a blade piercing his chest.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to force Weicheng to submit; he shouted curses at them and was run through the chest.

sentences.zh: 賊遂驅婦女墮城，稍緩，輒斷其腕，血淋漓土石間。

translations.literal: The bandits then drove the women to leap from the walls; if they hesitated even slightly, their wrists were severed, and blood streamed over the earth and stones.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then drove the captive women to hurl themselves from the walls; any who hesitated had their wrists cut off, and blood ran over the earth and stones.

sentences.zh: 三日而城平，復殺之以實塹焉。

translations.literal: In three days the walls were leveled; they were killed again to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days the walls were demolished, and the dead were piled into the moat to fill it.

sentences.zh: 自一，光山人。

translations.literal: Ziyi was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ziyi was from Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 謝廷讃，字曰可，金谿人。

translations.literal: Xie Tingzan, styled Yueke, a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tingzan (Yueke), from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 父相，由鄉舉為東安知縣。

translations.literal: His father Xiang, through the provincial examination, became magistrate of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang, a provincial graduate, served as magistrate of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 初，歲饑，吏偽增戶口冒振，繼者遂按籍征賦，民困甚。

translations.literal: At first, in a year of famine, clerks falsely inflated household registers to claim relief grain; successors then levied taxes according to the registers, and the people were sorely distressed.
translations.idiomatic: During an early famine, clerks had falsified household registers to claim relief grain; later officials taxed according to those inflated rolls, and the people were sorely burdened.

sentences.zh: 相為請，得減戶千三百。

translations.literal: Xiang petitioned on their behalf and obtained a reduction of 1,300 households.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang petitioned on their behalf and secured a reduction of 1,300 households from the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 奸人殺四人，棄其屍，獄三年不決。

translations.literal: Evildoers killed four people and abandoned their corpses; the case went unresolved in court for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Evildoers murdered four people and abandoned the bodies; the case remained unresolved in court for three years.

sentences.zh: 相禱於神，得屍所在，獄遂成。

translations.literal: Xiang prayed to the spirits and obtained the location of the corpses; the case was then concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang prayed to the spirits, discovered where the bodies lay, and the case was finally closed.

sentences.zh: 廷贊舉萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: Tingzan passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 26.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tingzan passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 26.

sentences.zh: 未授官，即極論礦稅之害。

translations.literal: Before receiving an appointment, he immediately argued to the utmost against the harm of mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Even before receiving an appointment, he submitted a forceful memorial against the evils of mining levies.

sentences.zh: 旋授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔二十八年春舉行冊立、冠婚之禮。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict had ordered that in the spring of Wanli 28 the rites of investiture, capping, and marriage be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an edict had called for the rites of investiture, capping, and marriage to be held in the spring of Wanli 28.

sentences.zh: 將屆期，都御史溫純、禮科給事中楊天民、御史馮應鳳相繼言，不報。

translations.literal: As the deadline approached, Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun, Supervising Secretary Yang Tianmin of the Bureau of Rites, and Censor Feng Yingfeng spoke in succession; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: As the deadline approached, Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun, Supervising Secretary Yang Tianmin in the Bureau of Rites, and Censor Feng Yingfeng remonstrated in turn, all to no reply.

sentences.zh: 廷贊上疏言閣員當補，臺省當選，礦稅當撤，冠婚、冊立當速，詔令當信。

translations.literal: Tingzan submitted a memorial stating that grand secretaries ought to be filled, censorate and supervising secretaries ought to be selected, mining taxes ought to be withdrawn, capping, marriage, and investiture ought to be hastened, and edicts ought to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tingzan submitted a memorial urging that grand secretaries be appointed, censorate and supervising secretaries be chosen, mining levies be abolished, capping, marriage, and investiture be expedited, and imperial edicts be honored.

sentences.zh: 持疏跪文華門，候命逾時。

translations.literal: Holding his memorial, he knelt at the Wenhua Gate and waited for orders beyond the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial in hand, he knelt at the Wenhua Gate and waited long past the appointed hour.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，遣中官田義詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and dispatched the eunuch Tian Yi to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sent the eunuch Tian Yi to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 趙數日，命大學士趙誌臯、沈一貫擬敕諭，令禮部具儀。

translations.literal: After several days, he ordered Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan to draft an edict of instruction, directing the Ministry of Rites to prepare the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later, he ordered Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan to draft an edict instructing the Ministry of Rites to prepare the ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 比擬諭進，竟不發。

translations.literal: When the draft edict was submitted, it was ultimately not issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the draft edict was submitted, it was never issued.

sentences.zh: 誌臯、一貫趣之，帝乃言因廷贊出位邀功，以致少待，命示諸司靜俟。

translations.literal: Zhigao and Yiguan pressed him; the emperor then said that because Tingzan had overstepped his place to claim credit, there would be a brief delay, and ordered the offices to wait quietly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan pressed the matter, but the emperor replied that because Xie Tingzan had overstepped his bounds to claim credit, matters would be held briefly, and ordered the ministries to wait quietly.

sentences.zh: 遂褫廷贊職為民，並奪尚書蕭大亨，侍郎邵傑、董裕俸一歲，貶郎中徐如珂、員外郎林耀，主事鐘鳴陛、曹文偉三秩，調極邊。

translations.literal: Tingzan was then stripped of office and made a commoner; Minister Xiao Daheng and Vice Ministers Shao Jie and Dong Yu had their salaries withheld for one year; Directors Xu Ruke and Vice Director Lin Yao and Secretaries Zhong Mingbi and Cao Wenwei were demoted three ranks and transferred to the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tingzan was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status; Minister Xiao Daheng and Vice Ministers Shao Jie and Dong Yu had their salaries suspended for a year; Directors Xu Ruke and Lin Yao and Secretaries Zhong Mingbi and Cao Wenwei were demoted three ranks and posted to the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 是歲冊立之禮不行，廷贊歸。

translations.literal: That year the rite of investiture was not carried out, and Tingzan returned home.
translations.idiomatic: That year the investiture ceremony was not held, and Xie Tingzan returned home.

sentences.zh: 僑寓維揚，授徒自給。

translations.literal: He sojourned in Weiyang and supported himself by teaching disciples.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in exile at Yangzhou and supported himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈尚寶卿。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously awarded Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 兄廷諒，字友可。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tingliang, styled Youke.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xie Tingliang (Youke).

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 23.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Wanli 23.

sentences.zh: 授南京刑部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝命李廷機入閣，又召王錫爵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Li Tingji to enter the Grand Secretariat and also summoned Wang Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Tingji into the Grand Secretariat and also recalled Wang Xijue.

sentences.zh: 廷諒言：「廷機才弱而暗，錫爵氣高而揚，均不宜用。

translations.literal: Tingliang said: "Tingji's talent is weak and obscure; Xijue's spirit is lofty and overbearing—neither should be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tingliang wrote: "Li Tingji's talent is feeble and obscure; Wang Xijue's manner is proud and overbearing—neither is fit for office.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「儲君之立為王也，自錫爵始；

translations.literal: He also said: "The heir's establishment as king began with Xijue;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The heir's designation as king began with Wang Xijue;

sentences.zh: 舉人之有考察也，自廷機始；

translations.literal: The evaluation of provincial graduates began with Tingji;
translations.idiomatic: The practice of evaluating provincial graduates began with Li Tingji;

sentences.zh: 巡按之久任也，自趙世卿始；

translations.literal: The long tenure of touring censors began with Zhao Shiqing;
translations.idiomatic: The long tenure of touring censors began with Zhao Shiqing;

sentences.zh: 章疏之留中也，自申時行始；

translations.literal: The holding back of memorials in the palace began with Shen Shixing;
translations.idiomatic: The practice of withholding memorials in the palace began with Shen Shixing;

sentences.zh: 年例之不舉，考察之不下也，自沈一貫始。

translations.literal: The failure to hold the annual review and to issue evaluations began with Shen Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: The neglect of annual reviews and the failure to issue official evaluations began with Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 此皆亂人國者也。

translations.literal: These are all things that disorder the state.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were practices that threw the state into disorder.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，留中。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was held back in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, it was withheld.

sentences.zh: 終順慶知府。

translations.literal: He ended as prefect of Shunqing.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Shunqing.

sentences.zh: 楊天民，字正甫，山西太平人。

translations.literal: Yang Tianmin, styled Zhengfu, a native of Taiping in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianmin (Zhengfu), from Taiping in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 17.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Wanli 17.

sentences.zh: 除朝城知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Chaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Chaocheng.

sentences.zh: 調繁諸城，有異政，擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: Transferred to the demanding post of Zhucheng, he had outstanding administration and was promoted supervising secretary of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the demanding county of Zhucheng, he distinguished himself in office and was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時方纂修國史，與御史牛應元請復建文年號，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the national history was being compiled; together with Censor Niu Yingyuan he requested restoration of the Jianwen reign title, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: While the national history was being compiled, he and Censor Niu Yingyuan petitioned to restore the Jianwen reign title, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，狄道山崩，下成池，山南湧大小山五。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, a mountain at Didao collapsed, forming a pool below; south of the mountain five large and small hills surged up.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 27 a mountain at Didao collapsed, forming a pool below, while five hills large and small rose up to its south.

sentences.zh: 天民言：「平地成山，惟唐垂拱間有之，而唐遂易為周。

translations.literal: Tianmin said: "Mountains forming on level ground occurred only during the Chuigong era of Tang, and Tang was then changed to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianmin wrote: "Mountains rising on level ground occurred only once before, in the Chuigong era of Tang—and Tang was then overthrown and replaced by Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今虎狼之使吞噬無窮，狗鼠之徒攘奪難厭。

translations.literal: Today tiger-and-wolf emissaries devour without end, and dog-and-rat minions seize and plunder without satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Today wolfish emissaries devour without end, and verminous underlings plunder without satiety.

sentences.zh: 不市而征稅，無礦而輸銀。

translations.literal: Without markets they levy taxes; without mines they demand silver.
translations.idiomatic: They levy taxes where there is no commerce and demand silver where there are no mines.

sentences.zh: 甚且毀廬壞冢，籍人貲產，非法行刑。

translations.literal: They even destroy dwellings and tombs, confiscate people's property, and punish by illegal execution.
translations.idiomatic: They even demolish homes and desecrate graves, seize people's property, and punish by unlawful execution.

sentences.zh: 自大吏至守令，每被譴逐。

translations.literal: From high officials down to magistrates and prefects, many are rebuked and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: From senior officials down to local magistrates, many are rebuked and driven from office.

sentences.zh: 郡邑不肖者，反助虐交歡，藉潤私橐。

translations.literal: Unworthy prefects and magistrates instead help the cruel and make merry with them, borrowing [from the oppression] to fill their private purses.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy local officials abetted the cruelty instead, fraternizing with the oppressors and padding their own pockets.

sentences.zh: 嗷嗷之眾，益無所歸命，懷樂禍心，有土崩之勢。

translations.literal: The wailing masses increasingly have nowhere to turn for protection, harbor hearts that rejoice at disaster, and show signs of the realm crumbling like earth.
translations.idiomatic: The suffering populace, with nowhere left to turn, nursed hearts eager for calamity—a state verging on collapse.

sentences.zh: 天心仁愛，亟示譴告，陛下尚不覺悟，翻然與天下更始哉！

translations.literal: Heaven's heart is benevolent and has repeatedly shown warnings and rebukes—will Your Majesty still fail to awaken and turn about to renew the realm with the people!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven in its compassion has again and again sent warnings and reproof; will Your Majesty still not awaken and turn to make a fresh start with the realm?

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 文選郎中梅守峻貪黷，將擢太常少卿，天民劾罷之。

translations.literal: Mei Shoujun, director in the Bureau of Appointments, was corrupt; about to be promoted Vice Minister of Ceremonies—Tianmin impeached him and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Shoujun, a director in the Bureau of Appointments, was corrupt and on the verge of promotion to Vice Minister of Ceremonies; Yang Tianmin impeached him and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 延綏總兵官趙夢麟潛師襲寇，以大捷聞，督撫李汶、王見賓等鹹進秩予蔭。

translations.literal: Zhao Menglin, regional commander of Yan-sui, secretly led troops to attack bandits and reported a great victory; the governors-general Li Wen, Wang Jianbin, and others all received rank advancement and hereditary privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Menglin, regional commander of Yan-sui, launched a secret strike against the bandits and reported a great victory; the governors Li Wen, Wang Jianbin, and others were all promoted and granted hereditary privileges.

sentences.zh: 寇乃大入，殺軍民萬計，汶等又妄奏捷。

translations.literal: The bandits then made a major incursion, killing military and civilians by the tens of thousands; Wen and the others again falsely reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then swept in on a large scale, slaughtering tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians; Wen and the others again falsely claimed victory.

sentences.zh: 天民再疏論之，奪見賓職，夢麟戍邊，汶亦被譴。

translations.literal: Tianmin memorialized again arguing the matter; Wang Jianbin was stripped of office, Menglin was sent to garrison the frontier, and Wen was also censured.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianmin memorialized again on the affair; Wang Jianbin was stripped of office, Zhao Menglin was banished to frontier garrison duty, and Li Wen was censured as well.

sentences.zh: 天民尋進右給事中。

translations.literal: Tianmin was soon promoted to right supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianmin was soon promoted to right supervising secretary in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 冊立久稽，再疏請，不報。

translations.literal: Formal investiture long delayed, he memorialized again requesting it; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture of the heir had long been postponed; he memorialized again to urge it, to no reply.

sentences.zh: 無何，貴妃弟鄭國泰疏請皇長子先冠婚後冊立，天民斥其非。

translations.literal: Before long, the imperial consort's brother Zheng Guotai memorialized asking that the eldest imperial son first receive capping and marriage before investiture; Tianmin denounced this as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Zheng Guotai, brother of the favored consort, memorialized asking that the eldest imperial son be capped and married before formal investiture; Yang Tianmin denounced the proposal.

sentences.zh: 國泰懼，委罪都指揮李承恩，奪其俸。

translations.literal: Guotai feared and shifted blame to Commander Li Chen'en, stripping his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai, alarmed, shifted the blame onto Commander Li Chen'en and had his salary confiscated.

sentences.zh: 順天、湖廣鄉試文多用二氏語，天民請罪考官楊道賓、顧天飐等，疏留中。

translations.literal: Provincial examination essays in Shuntian and Huguang heavily used the language of the Two Teachings; Tianmin requested punishment for examiners Yang Daobin, Gu Tianran, and others; the memorial was held at court.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examination essays in Shuntian and Huguang were riddled with Buddhist and Daoist phrasing; Yang Tianmin called for the examiners Yang Daobin, Gu Tianran, and others to be punished, but the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 二十九年五月，天民復偕同官上言，請早定國本。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-ninth year, Tianmin again joined colleagues in submitting a memorial asking early establishment of the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Wanli 29, Yang Tianmin again joined his colleagues in memorializing for an early decision on the heir.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謫天民及王士昌雜職，余奪俸一年，以士昌亦給事禮科也。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, demoted Tianmin and Wang Shichang to miscellaneous posts, and docked the rest one year's salary, as Shichang was also a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. He demoted Yang Tianmin and Wang Shichang to minor posts and docked the others' salaries for a year, since Shichang too served as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時御史周盤等公疏請，亦奪俸。

translations.literal: At the time Censor Zhou Pan and others jointly memorialized requesting it; they too had salaries docked.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zhou Pan and others had also submitted a joint memorial on the matter; their salaries were docked as well.

sentences.zh: 天民得貴州永從典史。

translations.literal: Tianmin received the post of registrar of Yongcong in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianmin was assigned the post of registrar of Yongcong in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 至十月，帝迫廷議，始立東宮，而天民等卒不召。

translations.literal: By the tenth month, the emperor, pressed by court debate, finally established the Eastern Palace, but Tianmin and the others were never recalled.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth month, pressed by debate at court, the emperor at last invested the Eastern Palace—but Yang Tianmin and the others were never recalled.

sentences.zh: 天民幽憤卒。

translations.literal: Tianmin died of hidden resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianmin died, consumed by bitter grief.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi era, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the title Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 初，天民去諸城，民為立祠。

translations.literal: Initially, when Tianmin left Zhucheng, the people built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Tianmin first left Zhucheng, the people erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 其後長吏不職，父老率聚哭祠下。

translations.literal: Afterwards, when chief officials were incompetent, elders would gather and weep beneath the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the local magistrates failed in their duties, village elders would gather to weep before his shrine.

sentences.zh: 何選，字靖卿，宛平人。

translations.literal: He Xuan, style Jingqing, was a native of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: He Xuan, styled Jingqing, came from Wanping.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Wanli 11.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Wanli 11.

sentences.zh: 除南昌知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Nanchang; summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Nanchang, then summoned to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 廷臣爭國本多獲譴，選語鄭貴妃弟國泰，令以朝野公論、鄭氏禍福懇言於貴妃，俾妃自請。

translations.literal: Court officials disputing the foundation of the state often received punishment; Xuan spoke with Zheng Guotai, brother of the imperial consort, and had him earnestly tell the consort of public opinion at court and beyond and the Zheng clan's fortune and disaster, so that the consort would request it herself.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials who pressed the heir question often met with punishment. He Xuan spoke with Zheng Guotai, brother of the favored consort, urging him to tell her plainly what court and country were saying and what fortune or ruin awaited the Zheng clan, so that she might petition on her own.

sentences.zh: 國泰猶豫，選厲色責之曰：「若不及今為身家計，吾儕群擊之，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: Guotai hesitated; Xuan sternly rebuked him, saying: "If you do not now plan for your family's safety, we will all attack together—it will be too late for regret.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai wavered. He Xuan rebuked him sternly: "If you do not act now to safeguard your house, we will all turn on you together—and then it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 」國泰懼，乃入告於妃，且疏請早定，以釋危疑。

translations.literal: " Guotai feared, entered and told the consort, and also memorialized asking early establishment to dispel danger and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Guotai went in to tell the consort and also memorialized for an early decision, hoping to dispel the crisis and uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 帝意不懌。

translations.literal: The emperor's mood was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 已，知出選指，深銜之。

translations.literal: Later, learning it came from Xuan's direction, he deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the advice had come from He Xuan, he nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吏部擬調驗封員外郎鄒元標於文選，疏六日不下，選以為言。

translations.literal: Before long the Ministry of Personnel proposed transferring Seal Verification division director Zou Yuanbiao to the Bureau of Appointments; the memorial six days was not issued, and Xuan spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Ministry of Personnel proposed transferring Zou Yuanbiao, a director in the Seal Verification division, to the Bureau of Appointments; the memorial languished six days without action, and He Xuan remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝憶前事，謫湖廣布政司照磨。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled the previous matter and demoted him to registrar in the Huguang provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling the earlier affair, the emperor demoted him to registrar in the Huguang provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 稍遷南京通政司經歷。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to administrator in the Nanjing Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to administrator in the Nanjing Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 刑部缺員外郎，吏部擬用選。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice lacked a director; the Ministry of Personnel proposed using Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When a directorship in the Ministry of Justice fell vacant, the Ministry of Personnel proposed appointing He Xuan.

sentences.zh: 帝憾未釋，謂特降官不當推舉，切讓尚書孫丕揚等，謫文選郎中馮生虞、員外郎馮養誌等極邊，而斥選為民。

translations.literal: The emperor's resentment undissolved; he said specially demoted officials should not be recommended, sharply rebuked Minister Sun Piyang and others, demoted Appointments director Feng Shengyu, director Feng Yangzhi, and others to the farthest frontier, and expelled Xuan to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's resentment had not faded. He declared that officials specially demoted should not be put forward, sharply rebuked Minister Sun Piyang and others, banished Appointments director Feng Shengyu, director Feng Yangzhi, and others to the remotest frontier, and stripped He Xuan of office entirely.

sentences.zh: 以閣臣言，稍寬生虞、養誌等罰。

translations.literal: On the Grand Secretaries' words, the punishments of Shengyu, Yangzhi, and the others were slightly eased.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Secretaries' urging, the punishments of Feng Shengyu, Feng Yangzhi, and the others were slightly reduced.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中任彥蘗抗章論救，語侵閣臣。

translations.literal: Nanjing supervising secretary Ren Yanbo submitted a forceful memorial arguing for rescue, with language impugning the Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yanbo, a supervising secretary in Nanjing, submitted a forceful memorial in their defense, his language impugning the Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 帝復怒，謫彥蘗於外，生虞仍以雜職調邊方。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry again, demoted Yanbo outside, and Shengyu was still transferred by a miscellaneous post to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged again. Ren Yanbo was demoted and transferred out; Feng Shengyu was still sent to the frontier in a minor post.

sentences.zh: 旋以言官論救，並斥彥蘗為民。

translations.literal: Soon, because censorial officials argued for rescue, Yanbo was also expelled to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When censorial officials again petitioned in his defense, Ren Yanbo too was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 於是御史許聞造上言：「陛下頃歲以來，謂公忠為比周，謂論諫為激擾；

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor Xu Wenzao memorialized: "Your Majesty these recent years treats public loyalty as factional collusion and treats remonstrance as inflammatory disturbance;
translations.idiomatic: Then Censor Xu Wenzao memorialized: "In recent years Your Majesty has treated public loyalty as factional collusion and remonstrance as inflammatory disturbance;

sentences.zh: 詘銓衡之所賢，撓刑官之所執。

translations.literal: You defeat what the Board of Personnel esteems and obstruct what judicial officials enforce.
translations.idiomatic: You override what the Board of Personnel recommends and obstruct what judicial officials uphold.

sentences.zh: 光祿太仆之帑，括取幾空；

translations.literal: The treasuries of the Imperial Household and the Court of the Imperial Stud have been nearly emptied by exactions;
translations.idiomatic: The treasuries of the Imperial Household and the Court of the Imperial Stud have been drained nearly dry;

sentences.zh: 中外大小之官，縣缺不補。

translations.literal: Officials great and small at court and beyond—county vacancies are not filled.
translations.idiomatic: Offices great and small, at court and in the provinces, go unfilled while county posts stand vacant.

sentences.zh: 敲撲遍於宮闈，桁楊接於道路。

translations.literal: Beatings and floggings spread through the inner palace; pillories and cangues line the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Beatings and floggings reach into the inner palace; pillories and cangues line the roads.

sentences.zh: 論救忠良，則愈甚其罪；

translations.literal: Argue to save the loyal and good, and their crimes are worsened;
translations.idiomatic: Plead for the loyal and upright, and their punishments grow harsher;

sentences.zh: 諫止貢獻，則愈增其額。

translations.literal: Remonstrate to stop tribute offerings, and the quotas are increased;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrate against levies and tribute, and the quotas are raised;

sentences.zh: 奏牘沈閣而莫稽，奄寺縱橫而無忌。

translations.literal: Memorials sink in the palace archives unexamined; eunuchs run rampant without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials sink into the palace archives unexamined, while eunuchs run rampant without restraint.

sentences.zh: 今欲摘陳一事，則慮陛下益甚其事；

translations.literal: Now, wishing to cite one matter, one fears Your Majesty will only intensify that matter;
translations.idiomatic: Now, to cite any one matter is to fear Your Majesty will only intensify it;

sentences.zh: 欲摘救一人，則慮陛下益罪其人。

translations.literal: Wishing to cite and save one person, one fears Your Majesty will only worsen that person's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: To plead for any one person is to fear Your Majesty will only deepen his guilt.

sentences.zh: 陛下執此以拒建言之臣，諸臣因此而塞進言之路。

translations.literal: Your Majesty holds to this to reject memorializing ministers; the ministers thereby block the path of speaking forth.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has used this to rebuff those who speak up, and ministers have closed the path of remonstrance in response.

sentences.zh: 邇年以來，諸臣謇諤之風，視昔大沮矣。

translations.literal: In recent years, ministers' forthright and blunt spirit, compared with former times, is greatly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the forthright spirit of the ministers has been crushed far below what it once was.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 生虞，大足人。

translations.literal: Shengyu was a native of Dazu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shengyu came from Dazu.

sentences.zh: 彥蘗，任城人。

translations.literal: Yanbo was a native of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yanbo came from Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈選光祿少卿，生虞太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi era, Xuan was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and Shengyu Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign, He Xuan was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and Feng Shengyu Vice Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：野史載神宗金合之誓。

translations.literal: Appreciation says: Unofficial histories record Shenzong's oath in a golden casket.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Unofficial histories tell of an oath Shenzong sealed in a golden casket.

sentences.zh: 都人子之說，雖未知信否，然恭妃之位久居鄭氏下，固有以滋天下之疑矣。

translations.literal: The tale among capital commoners, though its truth is unknown, yet Consort Gong's rank long below Lady Zheng's indeed gave grounds to breed realm-wide suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the tale told among the people of the capital is true cannot be known, yet Consort Gong's rank long stood below Lady Zheng's—enough in itself to feed suspicion throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 姜應麟等交章力爭，不可謂無羽翼功。

translations.literal: Jiang Yinglin and others submitting memorials in succession and vigorously disputing cannot be said to have had no supporting merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yinglin and others who submitted memorial after memorial in fierce dispute cannot be said to have lacked supporting merit.

sentences.zh: 究之鄭氏非褒、驪之煽處，國泰亦無駟、鈞之惡戾，積疑召謗，被以惡聲。

translations.literal: Investigated to the end, the Zheng clan was not in the inciting position of Bo and Li; Guotai also lacked the wicked violence of Si and Jun—accumulated suspicion invited slander, and they were clothed in ill repute.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Zheng clan was no Bo Si or Li Ji fomenting ruin, nor was Guotai as vicious as Zhao Chuan or Tian Fen; accumulated suspicion invited slander, and they were dressed in ill repute.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「時靡有爭，王心載寧。

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says: "Then none contend, and the king's heart finds peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "When none contend, the king's heart knows peace.

sentences.zh: 」諸臣何其好爭也！

translations.literal: " How contentious these ministers are!
translations.idiomatic: How eager these ministers are to quarrel!
